note: Verified field births and combinations from blind two-harvest runs per period (Wikipedia against MacTutor/SEP or Quanta/blogs), matched across lists and with the seed events, then judged by AI verifier passes. 1930-1990 and 1990-2026: an item counts as verified only if both a Sonnet pass and an Opus pass (with a bibliographic check of every main work) judged it real; items one pass accepted and one rejected are in `contestedOnly`. Before 1850: one Sonnet pass. 1850-1930: one Opus pass. Events dated near a boundary can appear in two periods. Not checked by a human.

events.name: Archimedes' mechanical method
events.summary: Heuristic balancing arguments from mechanics discovered areas and volumes, then proved by exhaustion.
keyWorks: Archimedes, The Method of Mechanical Theorems
Archimedes, Quadrature of the Parabola
events.verifierNotes: Archimedes' Method uses mechanical balance to find areas/volumes; text recovered 1906 but work c. 250 BCE. Duplicate of MA10.

events.name: al-Khwarizmi's algebra
events.summary: Al-Jabr treated linear and quadratic equations by standard reductions.
keyWorks: al-Khwarizmi, Al-Jabr wa'l-muqabala
events.verifierNotes: Al-jabr c. 820; algebra as independent discipline with geometric justification.

events.name: Analytic geometry (Descartes, Fermat)
events.summary: Geometric problems were translated into algebraic equations, solved and classified by degree.
keyWorks: Descartes, La Geometrie (1637)
events.verifierNotes: Canonical fusion of algebra and geometry; Fermat's Isagoge (c.1636) parallel.

events.name: Calculus (Newton, Leibniz)
events.summary: Tangent and area problems were unified as inverse operations with algorithms.
keyWorks: Newton, Methodus Fluxionum et Serierum Infinitarum (1671)
Leibniz, Nova methodus pro maximis et minimis (1684)
events.verifierNotes: Calculus; Newton's Methodus written 1671, published 1736. Duplicate of MA66. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Probability: Pascal-Fermat
events.summary: Correspondence solved the problem of points using expected value and combinatorics.
keyWorks: Pascal-Fermat correspondence (1654)
Huygens, De ratiociniis in ludo aleae (1657)
events.verifierNotes: Pascal-Fermat 1654 correspondence on division of stakes, Huygens 1657; standard birth of mathematical probability. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Graph theory: Konigsberg
events.summary: Euler abstracted the bridge problem to a network and decided it.
keyWorks: Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (1736)
events.verifierNotes: Seven bridges memoir published 1741 in Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 8. Duplicate of MA78. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Analytic number theory: Euler and Dirichlet
events.summary: Euler used continued fractions and series for Fermat's results and first steps toward analytic methods.
keyWorks: Euler, Variae observationes circa series infinitas (1737)
events.verifierNotes: Euler product and infinitude of primes via zeta (Variae observationes circa series infinitas, presented 1737, published 1744); Basel 1735. Clear analysis-to-number-theory transfer. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Group theory from equations (Lagrange to Galois)
events.summary: Resolvents and symmetric functions of roots were studied under permutations.
keyWorks: Lagrange, Reflexions sur la resolution algebrique (1770)
Vandermonde (1771)
events.verifierNotes: Lagrange 1770-71 Reflexions and Vandermonde 1771 analyse resolvents via permutations; direct precursor of group theory. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Fourier series
events.summary: Arbitrary functions were represented by trigonometric series to solve heat flow.
keyWorks: Fourier, Memoire sur la propagation de la chaleur (1807)
Fourier, Theorie analytique de la chaleur (1822)
events.verifierNotes: 1807 memoir and 1822 Theorie analytique: heat physics drives trigonometric-series expansion; standard.

events.name: Riemannian/intrinsic differential geometry
events.summary: Gaussian curvature and Theorema Egregium made curvature intrinsic.
keyWorks: Gauss, Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas (1827)
events.verifierNotes: Disquisitiones 1827 (publ. 1828); duplicate of MA91.

events.name: Ideals and algebraic number theory
events.summary: Failure of unique factorisation in rings of integers is repaired by introducing ideal elements, later recast as ideals, which become the central object.
keyWorks: E. E. Kummer, Zur Theorie der complexen Zahlen, J. reine angew. Math. 35 (1847) 319-326 (overview; proofs in the companion Uber die Zerlegung der aus Wurzeln der Einheit gebildeten complexen Zahlen in ihre Primfactoren, same volume, 327-367)
R. Dedekind, Supplement XI to Dirichlet's Vorlesungen uber Zahlentheorie (1871)
D. Hilbert, Die Theorie der algebraischen Zahlkorper (Zahlbericht, 1897)

events.name: Boolean algebra
events.summary: Logic was treated as an algebra of two values.
keyWorks: Boole, Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847)
events.verifierNotes: Boole's Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847), contemporary with De Morgan; algebra meets logic. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Oresme: graphing motion
events.summary: Uniform acceleration was studied and shown by area under a velocity diagram.
keyWorks: Nicole Oresme, graphical treatise
Swineshead, Liber calculationum
events.verifierNotes: Latitude of forms (Oresme, Tractatus de configurationibus, c.1350) plus Merton mean speed theorem (Heytesbury/Swineshead 1330s); geometry meets kinematics. Evidence URL (Mathematical analysis) is wrong; dates better 1328-1361. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Indian zero and place value
events.summary: Brahmi digits developed into a positional decimal system whose schools around 500-650 CE worked out place value and zero.
keyWorks: Aryabhata, Aryabhatiya (c. 499)
Brahmagupta, Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628)
events.verifierNotes: Positional decimal notation with zero is a genuine birth of written arithmetic; -250 start is unsupported. Same event as WA19. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Desargues projective geometry
events.summary: Properties invariant under projection, points at infinity and involution gave a unified theory of conics.
keyWorks: Desargues, Brouillon project (1639)
Bosse, perspective treatise (1648)
events.verifierNotes: Desargues Brouillon project (1639) unifies perspective and conics; standard birth of projective geometry. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Poncelet projective geometry
events.summary: Poncelet's treatise and the duality principle swapped points and lines.
keyWorks: Poncelet, Traite des proprietes projectives (1822)
Gergonne (1825)
events.verifierNotes: Poncelet 1822; Gergonne duality 1826 (Annales 16); birth of projective duality.

events.name: Fermat number theory
events.summary: Fermat's correspondence introduced the little theorem, four-square statement and other results.
keyWorks: Fermat, correspondence and marginalia
events.verifierNotes: Diophantus-reading marginalia c.1637, little theorem 1640, descent 1659; genuine founding of modern number theory. 'Correspondence and marginalia' fine; Observations on Diophantus were published 1670 by his son. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Indivisibles (Cavalieri)
events.summary: Cavalieri, Torricelli and Wallis computed areas by summing indivisible elements arithmetically.
keyWorks: Cavalieri, Geometria indivisibilibus (1635)
Wallis, Arithmetica Infinitorum (1656)
events.verifierNotes: Cavalieri 1635 + Wallis 1656 arithmetisation of quadrature; overlaps MA62.

events.name: Pascal's arithmetical triangle
events.summary: The triangle and induction were used to compute fair divisions.
keyWorks: Pascal, Traite du triangle arithmetique (1665)
events.verifierNotes: Same problem as WA45 (problem of points); merge into WA45. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Bernoulli Ars Conjectandi
events.summary: Bernoulli proved the first law of large numbers.
keyWorks: Jacob Bernoulli, Ars Conjectandi (1713)
events.verifierNotes: Ars Conjectandi 1713 (posth.); LLN plus first systematic probability; borderline internal.

events.name: Euler-Monge differential geometry of surfaces
events.summary: Clairaut, Euler and Monge studied curvature of curves and surfaces.
keyWorks: Clairaut (1731)
Euler (1760)
Monge, Application de l'analyse a la geometrie
events.verifierNotes: Clairaut 1731, Euler 1760 (printed 1767), Monge 1795/1807 form differential geometry of curves and surfaces. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Archimedes statics
events.summary: Archimedes treated equilibrium and floating bodies by geometric proof.
keyWorks: Archimedes, On the Equilibrium of Planes
Archimedes, On Floating Bodies
events.verifierNotes: Equilibrium of Planes and Floating Bodies mathematise mechanics; archetypal geometry-mechanics fusion. Dup of MA11. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Euler polyhedron formula
events.summary: A relation between numbers of vertices, edges and faces was found for convex polyhedra.
keyWorks: Euler, Elementa doctrinae solidorum (1758)
events.verifierNotes: V-E+F=2 as a topological invariant, published in Novi Comm. Petrop. 1758; standard start of topology (Descartes earlier, unpublished). (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Non-Euclidean geometry
events.summary: Rejecting the parallel postulate gave a consistent geometry.
keyWorks: Lobachevsky (Kazan Messenger, 1829)
Bolyai, Appendix (1831)
events.verifierNotes: Bolyai Appendix appeared 1832, not 1831. Genuine birth of non-Euclidean geometry; merge with WA74. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Islamic spherical trigonometry
events.summary: Islamic scholars used all six functions and proved spherical sine laws and identities.
keyWorks: Abu al-Wafa, trigonometric works
al-Jayyani, Book of Unknown Arcs of a Sphere
events.verifierNotes: Trigonometry becomes an independent discipline (Abu al-Wafa, al-Jayyani, and Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's treatise on the quadrilateral, c.1260 is the usual institutional marker). (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: al-Karaji polynomial algebra
events.summary: Algebra was freed from geometric operations, with powers and product rules defined for x and 1/x and polynomial arithmetic.
keyWorks: al-Karaji, al-Fakhri
al-Karaji, al-Badi
events.verifierNotes: Al-Karaji applies arithmetic operations to algebraic expressions (polynomial arithmetic, binomial coefficients, early induction); standard per Rashed. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Diophantus
events.summary: Arithmetica introduced symbols for unknowns and sought rational solutions to polynomial equations.
keyWorks: Diophantus, Arithmetica
events.verifierNotes: Arithmetica is syncopated algebra and indeterminate analysis; date uncertain. Reasonably a birth of Diophantine analysis. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Gauss Disquisitiones Arithmeticae
events.summary: Congruence notation, quadratic forms and cyclotomy were unified.
keyWorks: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801)
events.verifierNotes: Disquisitiones Arithmeticae: founding systematic number theory with congruences, reciprocity, cyclotomy. Duplicate of MA89. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Sharaf al-Din al-Tusi
events.summary: Existence of roots of cubics was analysed through maxima of polynomials.
keyWorks: Sharaf al-Din al-Tusi, al-Mu'adalat
events.verifierNotes: Sharaf al-Tusi's use of maxima to decide cubic solvability (Rashed) is contested as 'calculus'; 'algebraic geometry' target is an overreach. Date 1135 is a guess. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Indian indeterminate/Pell equations
events.summary: Integer solutions of equations of the form N x^2 + 1 = y^2 were found by composition and cyclic methods, including the case 61 with a very large minimal solution.
keyWorks: Brahmagupta, Brahmasphutasiddhanta (628)
Bhaskara II, Bijaganita (1150)
events.verifierNotes: Pell-type equation methods (bhavana composition, chakravala) are a genuine early indeterminate-analysis development. Related to WA21. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Complex numbers from the cubic
events.summary: Square roots of negatives appeared in the cubic formula and Bombelli formulated rules for them.
keyWorks: Cardano, Ars Magna
Bombelli, L'Algebra (1572)
events.verifierNotes: Cardano 1545 meets sqrt(-1), Bombelli 1572 gives rules; genuine emergence of complex numbers. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Ptolemy's Almagest
events.dates: Hipparchus c.-140, Menelaus c.100, Ptolemy c.150
events.summary: Ptolemy extended chord tables with sum, difference and half-angle formulas for astronomical computation.
keyWorks: Ptolemy, Almagest
events.verifierNotes: Direction is reversed: Almagest builds chord trigonometry from geometry for astronomy; Hipparchus and Menelaus precede. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Hipparchus chord table
events.summary: Astronomical needs led Hipparchus to tabulate chords of angles in a circle.
keyWorks: Hipparchus, table of chords (lost)
events.verifierNotes: Standard histories: Hipparchus' chord table c. 140 BCE; work lost, known via Ptolemy/Theon. Astronomy-geometry fusion.

events.name: Cauchy complex analysis
events.summary: Integrals along paths in the complex plane gave theorems and the calculus of residues.
keyWorks: Cauchy, Memoire sur les integrales definies (1814)
events.verifierNotes: Memoir presented 1814, printed 1827; imaginary-limit integrals 1825; residues 1826-27. Fusion of real integral calculus with complex variables. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Kerala series
events.summary: Madhava and followers derived series for sine, cosine and arctangent.
keyWorks: Madhava (attributed)
Neelakanta, Tantrasangraha
Jyesthadeva, Yuktibhasa
events.verifierNotes: Madhava's sine/cosine/arctan series; real transfer of infinite-series methods to trig functions. Yuktibhasa dated c.1530.

events.name: Laplace analytic probability
events.summary: Generating functions and asymptotic approximations were used to solve probability problems.
keyWorks: Laplace, Theorie analytique des probabilites (1812)
events.verifierNotes: Laplace's generating functions and analytic methods in probability; Memoire 1774/1782, Theorie analytique 1812.

events.name: Bayes inverse probability
events.summary: Bayes derived a posterior for the binomial.
keyWorks: Bayes (1763)
events.verifierNotes: Bayes' Essay in Phil. Trans. 53 (1763), communicated by Price; inverse probability. Duplicate of MA76.

events.name: Least squares
events.summary: Fitting observations by minimising squared errors predicted Ceres.
keyWorks: Gauss, Theoria combinationis (1823)
events.verifierNotes: Least squares combines probability and error theory with astronomy; Legendre published first in 1805, Gauss 1809/1823.

events.name: Newton's Principia
events.summary: Central-force motion, universal gravitation and orbit theory were derived by geometric mathematics.
keyWorks: Newton, Principia (1687)
events.verifierNotes: Principia founds mathematical dynamics via geometry; borderline since much is physics, but it created mathematical mechanics.

events.name: Euclid's Elements
events.summary: Results from earlier geometers were arranged as proofs from stated definitions, postulates and common notions in one treatise.
keyWorks: Euclid, Elements (c. 300 BCE)
events.verifierNotes: Elements c.300 BCE organises geometry, proportion and number theory axiomatically; genuine methodological birth, though 'to: mathematics' is vague.

events.name: Grassmann
events.summary: Grassmann built an algebra of extension.
keyWorks: Grassmann, Die lineale Ausdehnungslehre (1844)
events.verifierNotes: Ausdehnungslehre 1844 abstracts vector spaces and exterior algebra from geometry.

events.name: Lagrange analytical mechanics
events.summary: Mechanics was reduced to analysis based on virtual velocities, with no diagrams.
keyWorks: Lagrange, Mecanique analytique (1788)
events.verifierNotes: Variational principles and analysis recast mechanics; 1788 landmark.

events.name: Khayyam cubics via conics
events.summary: Cubics were classified and solved geometrically through intersections of conics, with a claim that ruler and compass are insufficient.
keyWorks: Omar Khayyam, Treatise on Demonstration of Problems of Algebra (c. 1070)
events.verifierNotes: Khayyam solves cubics by intersecting conics, c.1070-74.

events.name: Chinese remainder theorem
events.summary: A single-remainder puzzle grew into a general method for systems of congruences, including non-coprime moduli, motivated by calendar calculation.
keyWorks: Sunzi suanjing (c. 400-460)
Qin Jiushao, Shushu jiuzhang (1247)
events.verifierNotes: Calendar congruence problems lead to CRT (Sunzi) and general Da yan rule (Qin 1247).

events.name: Brachistochrone and calculus of variations
events.summary: Extremal problems for curves emerged from Newton's resistance and the Bernoullis' brachistochrone; Euler named the field.
keyWorks: Johann Bernoulli (1696)
Euler, Elementa Calculi Variationum
events.verifierNotes: Bernoulli's 1696 challenge launches calculus of variations; Euler 1744. Duplicate of MA73; conceptual start is 1696 not 1687.

events.name: Quintic impossibility
events.summary: Ruffini used permutation groups and Abel gave a complete proof of unsolvability of quintic.
keyWorks: Ruffini (1799)
Abel (1824)
events.verifierNotes: Ruffini 1799 (gap) then Abel 1824 pamphlet; permutation ideas applied to solvability. Overlaps MA98 (duplicate).

events.name: Monge descriptive geometry
events.summary: Monge turned military engineering projections into a geometric discipline.
keyWorks: Monge, Geometrie descriptive (1799)
events.verifierNotes: Monge's 1795 Ecole Normale lectures, publ. 1799; engineering/fortification drawing turned into a geometric theory.

events.name: Viete symbolic algebra
events.summary: Letters were used for both unknown and known quantities in a systematic method for equations.
keyWorks: Viete, In artem analyticem isagoge (1591)
events.verifierNotes: Isagoge 1591 symbolic algebra; duplicate of WA38 (merge).

events.name: Indian sine
events.summary: Siddhantic astronomy replaced chords by half-chords, giving the sine; Aryabhata tabulated it.
keyWorks: Aryabhata, Aryabhatiya
Surya Siddhanta
events.verifierNotes: Half-chord sine in Surya Siddhanta/Aryabhata; overlaps MA20 and MA13.

events.name: Euler's Introductio
events.summary: Functions replaced curves as the object of calculus, with e^{ix} relation, exponentials and logs.
keyWorks: Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748)
events.verifierNotes: Introductio 1748 makes the function the central object of analysis.

events.name: Napier's logarithms
events.summary: Napier linked arithmetic and geometric progressions to speed trigonometric calculation; Briggs made decimal tables.
keyWorks: Napier, Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio (1614)
Briggs, Logarithmorum Chilias Prima (1617)
events.verifierNotes: Napier 1614 fuses arithmetic/geometric progressions with trigonometry; Briggs 1617. Duplicate of MA49.

events.name: Hamiltonian optics and mechanics
events.summary: A function from ray optics was used for dynamics.
keyWorks: Hamilton, Theory of Systems of Rays (1826)
Hamilton, On a General Method in Dynamics (1834)
events.verifierNotes: Hamilton's optics-to-dynamics transfer 1827-35; same as WA69, duplicate.

events.name: Leibniz combinatorial logic
events.summary: Leibniz proposed a calculus of reasoning by symbolic manipulation, largely unpublished.
keyWorks: Leibniz, calculus ratiocinator (unpublished)
events.verifierNotes: Leibniz's logical calculus from combinatorial ideas, 1666 onward; overlaps MA69, duplicate.

events.name: Fermat adequality
events.summary: An algebraic adequality rule found extrema and tangents of curves.
keyWorks: Fermat, Method for determining maxima and minima and tangents (c. 1636)
events.verifierNotes: Fermat's adequality method for extrema/tangents, circulated 1636-38 (Methodus c.1636); algebra-geometry transfer. Duplicate of WA41.

events.name: Seki: resultants, determinants, elimination
events.summary: Seki Takakazu found resultant and determinant in elimination.
keyWorks: Seki Takakazu (1683)
events.verifierNotes: Seki Kaifukudai no ho (1683) gives determinant/resultant elimination, independent of Leibniz 1693. Minor field but a real birth of determinant theory. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Interpolation and finite differences from Chinese astronomy
events.summary: Second- and third-order difference methods in astronomy were later used by Zhu Shijie to sum sequences.
keyWorks: Liu Zhuo, Huangji calendar (c. 600)
Zhu Shijie, Siyuan yujian (1303)
events.verifierNotes: Astronomical computation gives finite-difference interpolation; Zhu Shijie extends to higher orders. Real but modest; Guo Shoujing missing from key works. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Numerical solution of polynomial equations in China (Ruffini-Horner)
events.summary: Root-extraction algorithms were extended step by step to cubics and higher-degree polynomial equations.
keyWorks: Wang Xiaotong (c. 600)
Qin Jiushao, Shushu jiuzhang (1247)
events.verifierNotes: Horner-type method is by Jia Xian/Liu Yi then Qin; Wang Xiaotong (c.626) only set up cubic equations. Borderline: algorithmic advance in algebra, kept at low confidence. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: De Moivre's formula: trigonometry and complex powers
events.summary: Powers of cos x + i sin x tie multiple-angle trigonometry to complex arithmetic.
keyWorks: De Moivre (1707 paper; 1722)
events.verifierNotes: Trig/complex-power link in De Moivre (1707, 1722) is real but in cubic-root form; modern formula due to Euler 1748. Weak claim. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Differential equations from calculus
events.summary: Newton solved fluxional equations by series; Leibniz separated variables; Bernoullis solved named equations.
keyWorks: Newton, Methodus Fluxionum (1671)
Jacob Bernoulli (1695)
events.verifierNotes: ODE as a theory emerges from fluxional equations, Leibniz 1691 separation, Bernoulli 1690-95; calculus plus mechanical problems. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Eudoxus theory of proportion
events.summary: A definition of equal ratio covering commensurable and incommensurable magnitudes let geometry compare any lengths, areas or volumes rigorously.
keyWorks: Eudoxus (reported in Euclid, Elements Book V)
events.verifierNotes: Eudoxus theory of proportion (Elements V) unifies commensurable and incommensurable magnitudes; high-confidence reification. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: De Moivre: normal approximation to the binomial
events.summary: Stirling-type asymptotics were applied to binomial sums, yielding the normal curve.
keyWorks: De Moivre, Approximatio (1733)
De Moivre, The Doctrine of Chances (1738, 1756)
events.verifierNotes: Approximatio of 1733 applies Stirling-type asymptotics to the binomial and gives first CLT case; privately printed 1733, in Doctrine of Chances 1738. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Jacobi: four squares via elliptic functions
events.summary: Jacobi derived the four-square theorem from theta functions.
keyWorks: Jacobi (1839)
events.verifierNotes: Four-square theorem via theta/elliptic functions is in Fundamenta nova (1829, par. 40-42), not 1839. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Taylor: finite differences and Taylor's theorem
events.summary: A treatise created the calculus of finite differences and gave the series later called Taylor's.
keyWorks: Taylor, Methodus incrementorum (1715)
events.verifierNotes: Methodus incrementorum directa et inversa (1715) founds finite-difference calculus and gives Taylor's formula as continuous limit of Newton interpolation. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Binomial coefficient triangle in China
events.dates: Jia Xian c.1050, Yang Hui 1261, Zhu Shijie 1303
events.summary: A table of binomial coefficients up to the eighth power appeared as the 'ancient method' of expanding powers.
keyWorks: Jia Xian (c. 1050, lost)
Zhu Shijie, Siyuan yujian (1303)
events.verifierNotes: Jia Xian's work is lost (known via Yang Hui); triangle appears earlier in India (Pingala/Halayudha) and in al-Karaji. Marginal event; low confidence. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Discovery of incommensurable magnitudes
events.summary: The failure of the hypotenuse of a right isosceles triangle to be a ratio of integers broke the identification of magnitude with number and forced a new foundation for geometry.
keyWorks: Pythagorean school (traditional attribution)
events.verifierNotes: Discovery of incommensurability is a real foundational event leading to Eudoxus; attribution and date are uncertain and sources are late. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Euler: geodesics from mechanics
events.summary: Euler derived the geodesic equation for motion on a surface.
keyWorks: Euler, Mechanica (1736)
events.verifierNotes: Euler's geodesic equation is in De linea brevissima (written 1728, printed 1732); Mechanica 1736 is not the source. Johann Bernoulli 1697 precedes. (checked from standard histories; no live request)

events.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi: trigonometry as independent discipline
events.summary: Al-Tusi's Quadrilateral treated plane and spherical trigonometry separately from astronomy.
keyWorks: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, Treatise on the Quadrilateral
events.verifierNotes: Tusi's Treatise on the Quadrilateral (c.1260) separates trigonometry from astronomy; standard split. Overlaps MA37.

events.name: Cotes: logarithm of complex arguments
events.summary: Cotes showed log(cos+i sin)=i theta.
keyWorks: Cotes, Harmonia Mensurarum (1714)
events.verifierNotes: Cotes' log formula is in Logometria (Phil. Trans. 1714); Harmonia mensurarum is posthumous 1722. Real log-trig link.

events.name: Hamilton: complex numbers as pairs and quaternions
events.summary: Complex numbers as ordered pairs, then non-commutative quaternions.
keyWorks: Hamilton (1833 Royal Irish Academy)
Hamilton, Lectures on Quaternions (1853)
events.verifierNotes: Complex numbers as ordered pairs and non-commutative quaternions; abstraction of algebra from geometry.

events.name: al-Mahani: geometric problems reduced to algebra
events.summary: Classical construction problems were recast as algebraic (cubic) equations.
keyWorks: al-Mahani (9th century)
events.verifierNotes: al-Mahani reduced Archimedes' sphere section/cube problems to a cubic equation; geometry to algebra bridge.

events.name: Abel: elliptic functions as inverses of elliptic integrals
events.summary: Inverting elliptic integrals gave doubly periodic functions.
keyWorks: Abel, Recherches sur les fonctions elliptiques (1827)
events.verifierNotes: Abel's inversion yields doubly periodic functions; genuine reorientation of integral calculus into function theory.

events.name: D'Alembert and Euler: wave equation and PDEs
events.summary: The vibrating string led to the wave equation and series solutions.
keyWorks: d'Alembert (1746)
Euler
D. Bernoulli
Lagrange
events.verifierNotes: Vibrating string produced the wave PDE; d'Alembert 1747 (Berlin Mem.), Euler, Bernoulli solution dispute.

events.name: Newton: infinite series and binomial theorem
events.summary: Expansion of non-integer powers and functions as series supplied tools for quadrature.
keyWorks: Newton, De Analysi per Aequationes Numero Terminorum Infinitas (1669)
events.verifierNotes: Binomial series and series methods of quadrature; De Analysi written 1669 (printed 1711).

events.name: Euclid Books VII-IX: arithmetic as a deductive theory
events.summary: Divisibility, the Euclidean algorithm and geometric progressions of integers were developed as a self-contained deductive body.
keyWorks: Euclid, Elements VII-IX
events.verifierNotes: Deductive arithmetic: Euclid VII-IX (divisibility, primes, Euclid's lemma); earliest number theory as theory.

events.name: Kepler's laws: conic geometry into planetary astronomy
events.summary: Planetary orbits became ellipses with area and period laws, replacing circle-based models.
keyWorks: Kepler, Astronomia nova (1609)
Kepler, Harmonices mundi (1619)
events.verifierNotes: Conics applied to planetary orbits: Astronomia nova 1609, Harmonices 1619; label should be astronomy/celestial mechanics.

events.name: Jacobi: theta functions and elliptic function theory
events.summary: Elliptic functions were rebuilt on theta functions in a systematic treatise.
keyWorks: Jacobi, Fundamenta nova (1829)
events.verifierNotes: Fundamenta nova (1829) theta functions used for sums of squares; a real transfer, not a reification.

events.name: Plucker: line geometry and algebraic curves
events.summary: Lines became elements of space and numerical characteristics of curves were related.
keyWorks: Plucker, Theorie der algebraischen Curven (1839)
events.verifierNotes: Plucker's duality, formulas and line coordinates; line geometry is mostly 1865+, institutional later.

events.name: Graunt: life tables
events.summary: Bills of mortality were analysed to build the first life table; Halley refined it.
keyWorks: Graunt, Natural and Political Observations (1662)
events.verifierNotes: Graunt's Observations on bills of mortality; Graunt did not use probability proper, so label should be statistics.

events.name: Clairaut: curves in space
events.summary: Analytic geometry and calculus were used to study curves of double curvature.
keyWorks: Clairaut, Recherches sur les courbes a double courbure (1731)
events.verifierNotes: Clairaut 1731 applies analytic geometry and calculus to space curves.

events.name: Geometric representation of complex numbers
events.summary: Wallis, Wessel, Argand and Gauss represented complex numbers as points in the plane.
keyWorks: Wessel (1799)
Argand (1806)
Gauss (1831)
events.verifierNotes: Wessel presented 1797 (published 1799); Argand 1806; Gauss 1831. Algebra to plane geometry bridge.

events.name: Huygens: evolutes and the isochronous pendulum
events.summary: The cycloid's tautochrone property and evolute theory tied curve geometry to pendulum clocks.
keyWorks: Huygens, Horologium oscillatorium (1673)
events.verifierNotes: Horologium oscillatorium 1673: evolutes, cycloidal pendulum; geometry of curves with mechanics.

events.name: Saint-Vincent and Sarasa: area under hyperbola and logarithm
events.summary: Area under the hyperbola was shown to behave as a logarithm; Leibniz tied log to the integral of dy/y.
keyWorks: Gregoire de Saint-Vincent (1647)
A. A. de Sarasa
events.verifierNotes: Saint-Vincent 1647 area under hyperbola, Sarasa 1649 logarithm link; real geometry-logarithm correspondence.

events.name: Islamic work on the parallel postulate
events.summary: Ibn al-Haytham, Khayyam and Tusi studied quadrilaterals as tests of the parallel postulate.
keyWorks: Ibn al-Haytham
Omar Khayyam
Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
events.verifierNotes: Ibn al-Haytham, Khayyam, Tusi on the fifth postulate; 1298 is dubious (Tusi died 1274).

events.name: Tian yuan: Chinese celestial-element algebra
events.summary: A positional notation for polynomials in an unknown, extended to four unknowns, let equations be set up and manipulated.
keyWorks: Li Zhi, Ce yuan hai jing (1248)
Zhu Shijie, Siyuan yujian (1303)
events.verifierNotes: Tian yuan polynomial notation on counting board (Li Ye 1248, Zhu 1303); Qin Jiushao 1247 is related.

events.name: Eudoxus method of exhaustion
events.summary: Inscribed polygons and double-contradiction arguments were used to prove volume ratios for pyramids, cones and the circle.
keyWorks: Eudoxus (reported in Euclid XII and Archimedes)
events.verifierNotes: Eudoxus exhaustion and proportion theory, known via Euclid XII/Archimedes; dates approximate.

events.name: Wallis: interpolation and infinite products
events.summary: Interpolating integer-power integrals gave an infinite product for pi.
keyWorks: Wallis, Arithmetica infinitorum (1656)
events.verifierNotes: Wallis 1656 interpolation and product for pi; duplicate of WA43 cluster (merge).

events.name: Pingala: combinatorics of poetic meters
events.summary: Counting patterns of long and short syllables yielded binomial-type identities and a binary-like device; Halayudha later described the triangle.
keyWorks: Pingala, Chandah Sutra
Halayudha, commentary on Chandah Sutra
events.verifierNotes: Chandahsutra dated c. 3rd-2nd c. BCE; enumeration of meters (prastara) is early combinatorics, expanded later by Halayudha.

events.name: Babylonian astronomical parameters enter Greek astronomy
events.summary: Greek geometric lunar models were tested and calibrated against Babylonian period parameters and eclipse records.
keyWorks: Hipparchus (lunar theory, as reconstructed)
events.verifierNotes: Hipparchus's use of Babylonian period relations; Toomer and Jones reconstructions.

events.name: al-Karaji: binomial coefficients and early induction
events.summary: A table of binomial coefficients and stepwise arguments for sums of integers and cubes anticipate induction.
keyWorks: al-Karaji, al-Badi
events.verifierNotes: Al-Karaji's arithmetisation of algebra and binomial/inductive argument; works only via later sources.

events.name: Ibn al-Haytham and Ibn Sinan: quadrature
events.summary: Sums of powers were used for areas and volumes, and Archimedean parabola quadrature was generalised.
keyWorks: Ibn al-Haytham, quadrature works
Ibrahim ibn Sinan, parabola quadrature
events.verifierNotes: Ibn Sinan (d. 946) and Ibn al-Haytham (c. 1020) quadratures with sums of powers; dates widened.

events.name: Arbuthnot: significance testing
events.summary: Arbuthnot used probability to argue birth ratios were not chance.
keyWorks: Arbuthnot (1710)
events.verifierNotes: Arbuthnot 1710 sex-ratio argument, early significance test; medium weight.

events.name: Hamilton's quaternions
events.summary: Hamilton found a noncommutative division algebra.
keyWorks: Hamilton (1843)
events.verifierNotes: Quaternions 1843 begin noncommutative algebra.

events.name: Lagrange: algebraic foundation for the calculus
events.summary: A programme grounded calculus on power series without limits or infinitesimals.
keyWorks: Lagrange, Theorie des fonctions analytiques (1797)
events.verifierNotes: Lagrange 1797 algebraic (power series) foundation of calculus; influential programme, borderline.

events.name: Kirchhoff: circuits and graphs
events.summary: Kirchhoff's circuit laws.
keyWorks: Kirchhoff (1845)
events.verifierNotes: Kirchhoff 1847 spanning-tree analysis of circuits; physics-to-graphs.

events.name: Abel's theorem and abelian integrals
events.summary: A theorem on sums of integrals of algebraic functions introduced genus, lost until 1952.
keyWorks: Abel, Paris memoir (1826)
events.verifierNotes: Abel's theorem presented 1826, published 1841; precursor of Jacobian/Riemann-surface theory.

events.name: Cardano: first treatise on chance
events.summary: Dice outcomes were analysed by counting favourable cases; the book appeared posthumously.
keyWorks: Cardano, Liber de ludo aleae (c. 1563; pub. 1663)
events.verifierNotes: Liber de ludo aleae written c. 1564, pub. 1663; precursor, pre-dates Pascal-Fermat; weak bridge.

events.name: Eudoxus homocentric spheres
events.summary: Planetary motion was modelled by nested rotating spheres whose combined motion produces the observed paths.
keyWorks: Eudoxus, On Velocities (lost)
events.verifierNotes: Eudoxus homocentric spheres known via Aristotle/Simplicius; geometric astronomy model.

events.name: De Moivre: chances and trigonometry/complex fusion
events.summary: De Moivre extended probability to approximation by analysis and linked powers of complex numbers to trigonometry.
keyWorks: de Moivre, Doctrine of Chances (1718)
de Moivre's formula (1730)
events.verifierNotes: Real event is the 1733 normal approximation (Stirling + binomial) in Doctrine of Chances 1738; complex-number formula not a probability bridge.

events.name: Babylonian quadratic and cubic problem-solving
events.summary: Questions about rectangle areas and excavation volumes were turned into procedures for solving quadratic and some cubic equations, without symbolic notation.
keyWorks: Old Babylonian tablets; BM 85200+ (cellar problems)
events.verifierNotes: Old Babylonian geometric-to-algebraic problem solving; 'birth of algebra' is contested (Hoyrup: cut-and-paste geometry), so treat as proto-algebra.

events.name: Perspective painting to projective geometry
events.summary: Brunelleschi, Alberti and Piero developed constructions of perspective later systematised geometrically.
keyWorks: Alberti, De pictura (1435)
Piero della Francesca, De prospectiva pingendi
events.verifierNotes: Brunelleschi c.1413, Alberti De pictura 1435, Piero: geometric theory of perspective; true projective geometry only with Desargues 1639.

events.name: Jaina permutations and combinations
events.summary: Jaina texts treated counting of permutations and combinations alongside multi-level infinities.
keyWorks: Jaina canon (Bhagavati Sutra tradition)
events.verifierNotes: Jaina combinatorics (permutations/combinations in Bhagavati Sutra) is genuine but the date -150 is a conventional guess; canon dating is uncertain.

events.name: Potential theory in celestial mechanics and physics
events.summary: The potential function and its equation were introduced for attracting masses, then used in electrostatics.
keyWorks: Laplace, Mecanique celeste (1799-)
Poisson (1813)
events.verifierNotes: Laplace potential 1782, Poisson 1813, Green 1828: mechanics+PDE yields potential theory as a field.

events.name: Gauss: fundamental theorem of algebra
events.summary: Gauss gave a largely topological proof; Argand gave another in 1806.
keyWorks: Gauss, doctoral dissertation (1797)
events.verifierNotes: Gauss thesis defended/published 1799 (Helmstedt), not 1797; uses geometric/continuity argument for algebraic theorem (with a topological gap).

events.name: Menelaus: spherical trigonometry
events.summary: Menelaus' Sphaerica gave theorems on spherical triangles.
keyWorks: Menelaus, Sphaerica
events.verifierNotes: Menelaus' Sphaerica (c.100 CE, survives in Arabic) founds spherical trigonometry in Greek geometry.

events.name: Euler: complex logarithms and exponentials
events.summary: Trigonometric and exponential functions were linked through complex arguments and logarithms of negatives.
keyWorks: Euler, Introductio (1748)
Euler, complex logarithms memoir (1751)
events.verifierNotes: Euler 1748 Introductio: exponential, trigonometric and complex numbers fused (Euler's formula); log of negatives 1749-51.

events.name: Mobius and Plucker: homogeneous coordinates
events.summary: Algebraic coordinates made duality and line geometry computational.
keyWorks: Mobius, Der barycentrische Calcul (1827)
Plucker, Analytisch-geometrische Entwickelungen (1828-31)
events.verifierNotes: Mobius 1827 and Plucker 1830-31 homogeneous coordinates marry analytic and projective geometry.

events.name: Leibniz: determinants
events.summary: Systems of linear equations were handled by an indexed notation for determinants, left unpublished.
keyWorks: Leibniz, manuscript of 22 January 1684
events.verifierNotes: Leibniz determinant ideas date from 1678-84 manuscripts; communicated in 1693 letter to l'Hopital; Seki independent 1683. Real but early linear algebra.

events.name: Viete: trigonometry applied to algebra
events.summary: A degree-45 equation posed by van Roomen was solved by recognising a trigonometric identity.
keyWorks: Viete, response to van Roomen (1595)
events.verifierNotes: Viete 1593-95 solves van Roomen's problem and cubics via trigonometry (angle sections).

events.name: Kepler: infinitesimal volumes of solids of revolution
events.summary: Volumes of revolved solids were found by summing infinitely many thin pieces.
keyWorks: Kepler, Nova stereometria doliorum (1615)
events.verifierNotes: Kepler Nova stereometria doliorum (1615) applies Archimedean infinitesimal methods to solids of revolution.

events.name: Eudoxus: theory of proportion and exhaustion
events.summary: Eudoxus gave a theory of ratios for incommensurables and the exhaustion method, a precursor of integration.
keyWorks: Eudoxus (via Euclid, Elements Book V)
events.verifierNotes: Eudoxus' proportion theory (Elements V) and exhaustion handle incommensurables; dates and attribution are reconstructed.

events.name: Transmission of Hindu-Arabic numerals to the Islamic world
events.summary: A treatise on Indian decimal calculation, later translated into Latin, spread the positional system and gave 'algorithm' its name.
keyWorks: al-Khwarizmi, On the Hindu numerals (Latin: Algoritmi de numero Indorum)
events.verifierNotes: Al-Khwarizmi's Indian-numerals book (c.820) is lost in Arabic; Latin Algoritmi is a 12th-c. translation. Transmission genuine but a borderline 'event'.

events.name: Pythagorean number theory and musical ratios
events.summary: Whole-number ratios behind consonant string lengths supported a programme of studying even, odd, triangular and perfect numbers as objects in themselves.
keyWorks: Pythagorean school, Croton (reported tradition)
events.verifierNotes: Pythagorean ratio-music link is traditional, only partly attested (Archytas/Philolaus); date uncertain.

events.name: Regiomontanus: trigonometry separated from astronomy in Europe
events.summary: De triangulis omnimodis presented trigonometry as a branch in its own right.
keyWorks: Regiomontanus, De triangulis omnimodis (1464)
events.verifierNotes: De triangulis written c.1464, printed 1533; first systematic trigonometry independent of astronomy in Europe.

events.name: Kolmogorov axiomatic probability
events.summary: Probability was grounded in measure theory, with events as sets and random variables as measurable functions.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (1933)
events.verifierNotes: Duplicate of WB1. English translation 1950 also confirmed.

events.name: Ergodic theory from statistical mechanics
events.summary: Koopman's operator on function spaces let von Neumann prove the first rigorous ergodic theorem.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis (PNAS 1932)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Koopman PNAS 1931 and von Neumann PNAS 1932 verified.

events.name: Computability theory (Church-Turing)
events.summary: Turing defined an abstract machine, computable numbers and a universal machine, answering the Entscheidungsproblem negatively.
keyWorks: Turing, On Computable Numbers (Proc. LMS 1936)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Turing, Proc. LMS 1936 verified via reprints.

events.name: Information theory
events.summary: Entropy and channel capacity were defined, with coding theorems for noisy communication.
keyWorks: Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (BSTJ 1948)
events.verifierNotes: BSTJ 1948 confirmed. Duplicate of WB14, merge.

events.name: Game theory
events.summary: The minimax theorem and an axiomatic treatment of economic behaviour created a mathematical theory of games.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele (1928)
von Neumann-Morgenstern, Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (1944)
events.verifierNotes: In scope (methodological 1944). Math. Ann. 1928 and the 1944 book are verified.

events.name: Probabilistic method
events.summary: Random constructions were used to prove existence of combinatorial objects.
keyWorks: Erdos, Some remarks on the theory of graphs (Bull. AMS 1947)
events.verifierNotes: Bull. AMS 53 (1947) confirmed.

events.name: Category theory
events.summary: Eilenberg and Mac Lane abstracted natural isomorphisms into functors and categories.
keyWorks: Eilenberg-Mac Lane, General theory of natural equivalences (1945)
events.verifierNotes: Eilenberg-Mac Lane 1945 confirmed (see WB6). Conceptual start 1942 (group extensions and homology). Duplicate of WB6.

events.name: Roth: Fourier analysis for progressions
events.summary: Circle method found progressions of length three in dense sets.
keyWorks: Roth, On certain sets of integers (1953)
events.verifierNotes: Roth, J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953) confirmed.

events.name: Sheaf theory
events.summary: Leray invents sheaves and spectral sequences to compute cohomology of fibrations.
keyWorks: Leray, Sur la forme des espaces topologiques, 1946
events.verifierNotes: The cited title is Leray, J. Math. Pures Appl. 24 (1945) 95-167 (written in captivity; confirmed via Numdam/MathSciNet). Sheaves and spectral sequences themselves first appear in Leray's 1946 Comptes Rendus notes, fully in 1950.

events.name: Schemes
events.summary: Spectra of arbitrary rings replaced varieties, unifying geometry over fields and over integers.
keyWorks: Grothendieck-Dieudonne, Elements de geometrie algebrique (1960-67)
events.verifierNotes: EGA I, Publ. IHES 4 (1960) confirmed. Fusion of commutative algebra with algebraic geometry; ICM 1958 announcement.

events.name: Weil conjectures
events.summary: Zeta functions of varieties over finite fields were conjectured to satisfy topological cohomological constraints.
keyWorks: Weil, Numbers of solutions of equations in finite fields (Bull. AMS 1949)
events.verifierNotes: Weil, Bull. AMS 55 (1949) confirmed.

events.name: Hilbert's tenth problem
events.summary: Exponential growth was shown Diophantine, proving undecidability of Diophantine equations.
keyWorks: Matiyasevich, Enumerable sets are Diophantine (1970)
events.verifierNotes: Doklady 191 (1970) 279-282 confirmed (web; JSL review). Davis-Putnam-Robinson 1961.

events.name: Atiyah-Singer index theorem
events.summary: The analytic index of elliptic operators was equated with topological invariants.
keyWorks: Atiyah-Singer, The index of elliptic operators I-V (Ann. Math. 1968-71)
events.verifierNotes: Announced Bull. AMS 1963; Ann. Math. 87 (1968) confirmed.

events.name: Langlands programme
events.summary: Conjectures tied automorphic representations of reductive groups to Galois representations and L-functions.
keyWorks: Langlands, Letter to Weil (1967)
Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms (1970)
events.verifierNotes: Langlands, LNM 170 (1970) confirmed; 1967 letter well documented.

events.name: Furstenberg ergodic Szemeredi
events.summary: Multiple recurrence in measure-preserving systems proved arithmetic progressions in dense sets.
keyWorks: Furstenberg, Ergodic behavior of diagonal measures (1977)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Furstenberg J. Anal. Math. 1977 verified.

events.name: Geometric group theory
events.summary: Hyperbolic groups bring negative-curvature geometry to finitely generated groups.
keyWorks: Gromov, Hyperbolic groups, 1987
events.verifierNotes: Gromov, 'Hyperbolic groups', MSRI Publ. 8 (1987) confirmed. Precursors Milnor/Svarc 1968, Gromov polynomial growth 1981.

events.name: Noncommutative geometry
events.summary: Geometry was extended to noncommutative C*-algebras.
keyWorks: Connes, Noncommutative differential geometry (1985)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Connes Publ. IHES 1985 verified.

events.name: Gauge theory and 4-manifolds (Donaldson)
events.summary: Instanton moduli spaces from physics' Yang-Mills equations restricted smooth four-manifold topology.
keyWorks: Donaldson, Self-dual connections and the topology of smooth 4-manifolds (Bull. AMS 1983)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Donaldson Bull. AMS 1983 verified.

events.name: Jones polynomial
events.summary: Braid group representations in von Neumann algebras produced a knot invariant.
keyWorks: Jones, A polynomial invariant for knots via von Neumann algebras (Bull. AMS 1985)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Jones Bull. AMS 1985 verified. Duplicate of WB95.

events.name: Symplectic topology (Gromov)
events.summary: Elliptic methods gave rigidity theorems.
keyWorks: Gromov, Pseudo holomorphic curves in symplectic manifolds (1985)
events.verifierNotes: Gromov, Invent. Math. 1985 confirmed. Elliptic PDE methods found symplectic topology.

events.name: Monstrous moonshine
events.summary: Monster group dimensions matched modular function coefficients.
keyWorks: Conway-Norton, Monstrous moonshine (1979)
events.verifierNotes: Conway-Norton, Bull. LMS 1979 confirmed. McKay's 1978 observation. Borcherds's 1992 proof.

events.name: Mirror symmetry
events.summary: Calabi-Yau dualities predict counts of curves.
keyWorks: Candelas et al., A pair of Calabi-Yau manifolds as an exactly soluble superconformal theory, 1991
events.verifierNotes: Candelas-de la Ossa-Green-Parkes, Nucl. Phys. B 359 (1991) confirmed; Greene-Plesser 1990 is the conceptual date.

events.name: Homological algebra
events.summary: Derived functors Ext and Tor were developed for modules over rings, extracted from topology.
keyWorks: Cartan-Eilenberg, Homological Algebra (1956)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Cartan-Eilenberg 1956 verified. Duplicate of WB8.

events.name: Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch and K-theory
events.summary: Grothendieck groups of coherent sheaves generalised Hirzebruch's Riemann-Roch theorem.
keyWorks: Borel-Serre, Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch (1958)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Borel-Serre Bull. SMF 1958 verified.

events.name: Thurston geometrisation
events.summary: Hyperbolic geometry was used to understand 3-manifolds via eight model geometries.
keyWorks: Thurston, Three-dimensional manifolds, Kleinian groups and hyperbolic geometry (Bull. AMS 1982)
events.verifierNotes: Bull. AMS 1982 confirmed. Hyperbolic geometry and Kleinian groups applied to 3-manifold topology; technique transfer or fusion fits better than dictionary.

events.name: Distributions
events.summary: Generalised functions were defined as continuous linear functionals on test functions, unifying Dirac delta, weak derivatives and Fourier transforms.
keyWorks: Schwartz, Theorie des distributions I-II (1950-51)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Schwartz 1945 Grenoble paper, 1948 survey and the treatise (1950-51) are confirmed via Crossref/Open Library.

events.name: Public-key cryptography
events.summary: Number-theoretic one-way functions enabled key exchange and signatures.
keyWorks: Diffie-Hellman, New directions in cryptography (1976)
Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (1978)
events.verifierNotes: Not an import from outside: number theory plus complexity yields public-key cryptography. Diffie-Hellman IEEE TIT 1976 confirmed. Duplicate of WB22.

events.name: Cobordism
events.summary: Manifolds up to cobordism were computed as homotopy groups of Thom spaces.
keyWorks: Thom, Quelques proprietes globales des varietes differentiables (1954)
events.verifierNotes: Thom, Comment. Math. Helv. 1954 confirmed. Homotopy theory of Thom spaces computes a differential-topology question.

events.name: Exotic spheres
events.summary: Seven-dimensional manifolds homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to the sphere were constructed.
keyWorks: Milnor, On manifolds homeomorphic to the 7-sphere (Ann. Math. 1956)
events.verifierNotes: Annals 1956 confirmed. Pontryagin classes plus Morse function construct exotic 7-spheres; duplicate of WB54, merge.

events.name: Higher algebraic K-theory (Quillen)
events.summary: Classifying space constructions defined higher K-groups.
keyWorks: Quillen, Higher algebraic K-theory I (1973)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Quillen LNM 341 (1973) verified.

events.name: Geometric invariant theory
events.summary: Quotients of varieties by group actions constructed moduli spaces.
keyWorks: Mumford, Geometric Invariant Theory (1965)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Mumford 1965 book verified.

events.name: Calabi conjecture
events.summary: Monge-Ampere equation solved to give Ricci-flat metrics.
keyWorks: Yau, On the Ricci curvature of a compact Kaehler manifold (1978)
events.verifierNotes: Yau, CPAM 1978 confirmed (PNAS announcement 1977). Nonlinear PDE settles a Kahler-geometry conjecture.

events.name: Quantum groups
events.summary: Hopf algebra deformations from Yang-Baxter.
keyWorks: Drinfeld (ICM 1986)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Drinfeld 1985 and Jimbo 1985; ICM 1986 Proceedings (1987) confirmed via Open Library.

events.name: Sullivan's dictionary
events.summary: Parallels between limit sets and Julia sets drove both fields.
keyWorks: Sullivan, Quasiconformal homeomorphisms and dynamics I (1985)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Sullivan Annals 1985 verified.

events.name: Entropy in ergodic theory
events.summary: Entropy becomes an isomorphism invariant of dynamical systems.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, 1958
Sinai, 1959
events.verifierNotes: Shannon entropy imported to settle isomorphism invariants of Bernoulli shifts; Kolmogorov Doklady 119 (1958) 861-864 confirmed (MathNet); Sinai 1959 confirmed via Selecta reprint.

events.name: Wavelets
events.summary: Morlet and Meyer link time-frequency analysis to orthonormal bases (Daubechies, Mallat).
keyWorks: Grossmann, Morlet, 1984
Daubechies, 1988
Mallat, 1989
events.verifierNotes: Grossmann-Morlet, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 1984 confirmed; Meyer 1985-86, Daubechies 1988, Mallat 1989.

events.name: Rational homotopy theory
events.summary: Differential algebras modelled rational homotopy types.
keyWorks: Sullivan, Infinitesimal computations in topology (1977)
events.verifierNotes: Publ. IHES 1977 confirmed. Quillen's Annals 1969 is the parallel, Lie-algebra model.

events.name: D-modules and Riemann-Hilbert
events.summary: Kashiwara and Bernstein turn PDE into module-theoretic questions; Riemann-Hilbert correspondence.
keyWorks: Kashiwara, 1975
Bernstein, 1972
Beilinson, Bernstein, 1981
events.verifierNotes: Real; Bernstein Funct. Anal. Appl. 1972 and Kashiwara 1978 verified (Kashiwara's 1970 thesis; Sato's school).

events.name: Faltings: Mordell conjecture
events.summary: Finiteness of rational points on curves of genus at least 2 is proved by combining the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties, moduli of abelian varieties and height theory.
keyWorks: G. Faltings, Endlichkeitssatze fur abelsche Varietaten uber Zahlkorpern, Invent. Math. 73 (1983) 349-366

events.name: Forcing and independence
events.summary: Cohen introduces forcing to build models in which CH or choice fails.
keyWorks: Cohen, The independence of the continuum hypothesis, PNAS 1963
events.verifierNotes: Forcing as a new method; Cohen PNAS 50 (1963) confirmed. Model theory input is modest; read as birth of forcing/independence methods.

events.name: Margulis superrigidity and arithmeticity
events.summary: Ergodic methods proved rigidity of lattices.
keyWorks: Margulis (1974-75)
events.verifierNotes: Margulis, ICM 1974 address confirmed (AMS Transl. 1977). Ergodic theory and boundary theory prove superrigidity and arithmeticity of lattices.

events.name: Supersymmetry and Morse theory
events.summary: Supersymmetric quantum mechanics gave a new proof of the Morse inequalities.
keyWorks: Witten, Supersymmetry and Morse theory (J. Diff. Geom. 1982)
events.verifierNotes: Witten, J. Diff. Geom. 17 (1982) confirmed.

events.name: Fourier integral operators and microlocal analysis
events.summary: Oscillatory integrals linking hyperbolic PDE to canonical transformations.
keyWorks: Hormander, 1971
Duistermaat, Hormander, 1972
events.verifierNotes: Duistermaat-Hormander, FIO II, Acta Math. 1972 confirmed (reprint). Same event as WB107 (microlocal analysis and FIO); merge.

events.name: High-dimensional Poincare and handle theory
events.summary: Handle decompositions of manifolds from Morse functions proved the generalised Poincare conjecture in dimensions at least five.
keyWorks: Smale, Generalized Poincare's conjecture in dimensions greater than four (Ann. Math. 1961)
events.verifierNotes: Smale, Ann. Math. 74 (1961) confirmed. Borderline intra-topology; counts as gradient-flow/handle technique settling Poincare n>=5.

events.name: Inverse scattering
events.summary: Schroedinger scattering solved the KdV equation.
keyWorks: Gardner-Greene-Kruskal-Miura (PRL 1967)
events.verifierNotes: Real; GGKM PRL 1967 and Lax CPAM 1968 verified.

events.name: Fermi-Pasta-Ulam and solitons
events.summary: Numerical experiments lead to the soliton concept.
keyWorks: Fermi, Pasta, Ulam, Studies of nonlinear problems, 1955
Zabusky, Kruskal, 1965
events.verifierNotes: Zabusky-Kruskal PRL 1965 confirmed; FPU 1955 Los Alamos report. Closely linked to WB83; could be merged.

events.name: Finite element method
events.summary: Piecewise polynomial trial spaces gave systematic solvers.
keyWorks: Turner et al. (1956)
Courant (1943)
events.verifierNotes: Turner-Clough-Martin-Topp 1956 confirmed; Courant Bull AMS 1943 confirmed. Duplicate of WB117, merge.

events.name: Kac-Moody algebras
events.summary: Generalised Cartan matrices gave infinite-dimensional algebras.
keyWorks: Moody (1968)
events.verifierNotes: Kac, Izv. 1968, and Moody, J. Algebra 1968, confirmed. Birth by abstraction; the later fusion with modular forms (Macdonald identities, Kac 1974) could be a separate event.

events.name: Yang-Baxter and solvable lattice models
events.summary: Yang-Baxter equation.
keyWorks: Baxter, Exactly Solved Models (1982)
events.verifierNotes: The key work is Baxter, 'Partition function of the eight-vertex lattice model', Ann. Phys. 1972 (Crossref); the 1982 book is a later summary. Yang 1967 plus Baxter 1971-72 give the Yang-Baxter equation, an import from statistical mechanics feeding later quantum groups.

events.name: Shannon switching circuits
events.summary: Boole's algebra was applied to analyse and simplify relay circuits.
keyWorks: Shannon, A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits (1938)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Shannon, Trans. AIEE 1938 verified.

events.name: Linear programming and simplex method
events.summary: An algorithm moving along vertices of a polyhedron solved linear programs efficiently.
keyWorks: Dantzig, Maximization of a linear function of variables subject to linear inequalities (1951)
events.verifierNotes: Dantzig's chapter in Koopmans (ed.), Activity Analysis 1951, confirmed via the volume. Simplex method 1947. Shares an event with MB16 (birth of LP).

events.name: Axiomatic homology
events.summary: Homology theories were characterised by axioms such as excision, allowing comparison and later generalised theories.
keyWorks: Eilenberg-Steenrod, Axiomatic approach to homology theory (PNAS 1945)
Eilenberg-Steenrod, Foundations of Algebraic Topology (1952)
events.verifierNotes: PNAS 1945 confirmed. Homology's methods turned into an axiomatic theory; tied to Eilenberg-Mac Lane 1945 category theory.

events.name: Coherent sheaves (FAC)
events.summary: Sheaf cohomology was imported into algebraic varieties over Zariski topology.
keyWorks: Serre, Faisceaux algebriques coherents (Ann. Math. 1955)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Serre Annals 1955 verified.

events.name: Weil foundations of algebraic geometry
events.summary: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil rebuild the Italian results over arbitrary fields.
keyWorks: Weil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, 1946
Zariski, 1935
events.verifierNotes: AMS Colloquium 29, 1946 confirmed. van der Waerden 1926 is out of scope but Zariski 1935-39 and Weil 1946 are within.

events.name: Etale cohomology
events.summary: Grothendieck topologies gave cohomology theories for varieties over finite fields as required by Weil.
keyWorks: Artin-Grothendieck-Verdier, SGA 4 (1963-64)
events.verifierNotes: SGA4 seminar 1963-64, published LNM 269/270/305 (1972-73), confirmed via Crossref.

events.name: Topological K-theory
events.summary: Vector bundle classes formed a generalised cohomology theory, used on Hopf invariant and index problems.
keyWorks: Atiyah-Hirzebruch, Vector bundles and homogeneous spaces (1961)
Atiyah, K-theory (1967)
events.verifierNotes: Atiyah-Hirzebruch, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 3 (1961) confirmed. Grothendieck's K-theory (1957) is the algebraic source.

events.name: Smale hyperbolic dynamics
events.summary: Topological methods were applied to structural stability, followed by strange attractors.
keyWorks: Smale, Differentiable dynamical systems (Bull. AMS 1967)
events.verifierNotes: Smale, Bull. AMS 1967 confirmed. Duplicate of WB79, merge.

events.name: Nash equilibrium
events.summary: Equilibria of non-cooperative games were shown to exist via fixed-point arguments.
keyWorks: Nash, Non-cooperative Games (thesis 1950)
events.verifierNotes: Nash, PNAS 1950 (reprints confirmed) and Annals 1951 confirmed. A fixed-point theorem from topology founds non-cooperative game theory.

events.name: KAM theory
events.summary: Diophantine conditions allow invariant tori to persist under perturbation of integrable systems.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, On conservation of conditionally periodic motions (1954)
events.verifierNotes: Kolmogorov, Doklady 1954 confirmed (English translation record). Moser 1962 and Arnold 1963 completed the proofs.

events.name: Hormander linear PDE
events.summary: Existence and regularity for general PDE are proved by Fourier and distribution methods.
keyWorks: Hormander, Linear Partial Differential Operators, 1963
Malgrange, Ehrenpreis, 1955
events.verifierNotes: Too vague as stated; recast as Malgrange-Ehrenpreis theorem (distribution theory/functional analysis settles existence of fundamental solutions). Hormander 1963 book confirmed (Open Library).

events.name: Pseudodifferential operators
events.summary: Symbol calculus extended Calderon-Zygmund theory to PDE, then to propagation of singularities.
keyWorks: Kohn-Nirenberg, An algebra of pseudo-differential operators (1965)
Hoermander, Analysis of Linear PDO III-IV (1985)
events.verifierNotes: 'From' was circular. Kohn-Nirenberg CPAM 18 (1965) confirmed; Hormander FIO 1971.

events.name: Catastrophe theory
events.summary: Singularity classification was proposed as a model of discontinuous change in morphogenesis.
keyWorks: Thom, Stabilite structurelle et morphogenese (1972)
events.verifierNotes: Real but faded field. Thom 1972 book verified (Open Library).

events.name: TQFT
events.summary: Chern-Simons theory interpreted the Jones polynomial and gave invariants of 3-manifolds.
keyWorks: Witten, Quantum field theory and the Jones polynomial (Comm. Math. Phys. 1989)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Witten CMP 1989 verified. Same event cluster as WB94/WB95.

events.name: Fractal geometry
events.summary: Self-similar sets with non-integer dimension were studied as models in nature and via computer experiments.
keyWorks: Mandelbrot, Les objets fractals (1975)
Mandelbrot, Fractal Geometry of Nature (1982)
events.verifierNotes: 'Les objets fractals' 1975 confirmed (Open Library). The listed 'complex dynamics' ingredient is anachronistic (Mandelbrot set 1980).

events.name: Recursion theory and realizability
events.summary: Recursive functions were used to interpret intuitionistic arithmetic.
keyWorks: Kleene, On the interpretation of intuitionistic number theory (1945)
events.verifierNotes: Kleene JSL 1945 verified. This is realizability (computability vs intuitionistic proof), not the birth of recursion theory. Duplicate of WB39.

events.name: Monte Carlo
events.summary: Random sampling was used on computers to solve deterministic problems.
keyWorks: Metropolis-Ulam, The Monte Carlo Method (JASA 1949)
events.verifierNotes: Metropolis-Ulam, JASA 1949 confirmed. Born in nuclear-weapons physics computation; Metropolis algorithm 1953.

events.name: Non-standard analysis
events.summary: Model-theoretic extension of the reals made infinitesimals rigorous.
keyWorks: Robinson, Non-standard analysis (1966)
events.verifierNotes: Robinson's book 'Non-standard analysis' confirmed (Crossref reprint; 1966 original). First paper is Proc. Kon. Ned. Akad. 1961. Model theory into analysis.

events.name: Computational complexity
events.summary: Resource-bounded computation was classified into hierarchies.
keyWorks: Hartmanis-Stearns, On the computational complexity of algorithms (1965)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Hartmanis-Stearns, Trans. AMS 1965 verified (1964 FOCS version). Cobham/Edmonds 1965 too.

events.name: NP-completeness
events.summary: Satisfiability was shown universal for NP, with many combinatorial problems reduced to it.
keyWorks: Cook, The complexity of theorem-proving procedures (STOC 1971)
Karp, Reducibility among combinatorial problems (1972)
events.verifierNotes: Cook, STOC 1971 confirmed; Karp 1972 not checked. Levin 1973 independent.

events.name: Kalman filter
events.summary: State-space recursive estimation unified filtering and control.
keyWorks: Kalman, A new approach to linear filtering and prediction problems (1960)
events.verifierNotes: Same 1960 paper as WB33; duplicate, merge.

events.name: Dynamic programming
events.summary: Principle of optimality recast multi-stage decisions as recursion.
keyWorks: Bellman, Dynamic Programming (1957)
events.verifierNotes: Duplicate of WB113. Book 1957 confirmed.

events.name: Tarski quantifier elimination
events.summary: Quantifier elimination showed the first-order theory of the reals is decidable.
keyWorks: Tarski, A decision method for elementary algebra and geometry (1948)
events.verifierNotes: Tarski 1951 book confirmed (1948 RAND report). Duplicate of WB87.

events.name: Algorithmic information theory
events.summary: Randomness was defined through shortest program length.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, Three approaches to the quantitative definition of information (1965)
Solomonoff (1964)
Chaitin (1966)
events.verifierNotes: Kolmogorov 1965 confirmed (Crossref has the 1968 reprint). Solomonoff 1964 and Chaitin 1966 independent.

events.name: Fuzzy sets
events.summary: Graded membership generalised set theory for imprecise concepts.
keyWorks: Zadeh, Fuzzy sets (Info. Control 1965)
events.verifierNotes: Information and Control 1965 confirmed. Genuine new area (MSC 03E72), though peripheral to core mathematics.

events.name: Gelfand theory of Banach algebras
events.summary: Maximal ideals of normed rings gave a topological representation.
keyWorks: Gelfand, Normierte Ringe (1941)
events.verifierNotes: Gelfand 'Normierte Ringe', Mat. Sb. 1941; Crossref returns the Collected Papers version ('Commutative normed rings'). Algebra (maximal ideals) and topology recast analysis; birth of Banach algebra theory.

events.name: Elementary topos theory
events.summary: Categories with subobject classifiers served as generalised universes of sets.
keyWorks: Lawvere-Tierney, elementary topoi (1970-71)
events.verifierNotes: Lawvere, 'Quantifiers and sheaves', Actes ICM Nice 1970 (pub. 1971) confirmed by web; Tierney LNM 274 (1972) confirmed.

events.name: Curry-Howard
events.summary: Proofs were matched with programs.
keyWorks: Howard, Formulae-as-types notion of construction (1969)
events.verifierNotes: Howard typescript 1969, published in To H.B. Curry (1980) 479-490, confirmed via web; Curry 1934/1958 precedent.

events.name: Domain theory
events.summary: Continuous lattices gave models for the lambda calculus.
keyWorks: Scott, Outline of a mathematical theory of computation (1970)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Scott 1970 Outline (Open Library) and Continuous lattices 1972 verified.

events.name: Formal language theory
events.summary: Grammar types were classified by automata.
keyWorks: Chomsky, Three models for the description of language (1956)
events.verifierNotes: Chomsky, IRE Trans. Inf. Theory 1956 confirmed. Chomsky 1959 and Chomsky-Schutzenberger 1963 consolidate it.

events.name: Ax-Kochen
events.summary: Ultraproducts showed Artin's conjecture on p-adic forms holds for large primes.
keyWorks: Ax-Kochen, Diophantine problems over local fields I-III (1965-66)
events.verifierNotes: Ax-Kochen I-III, AJM 1965 and Annals 1966, confirmed. Model theory settles an asymptotic version of Artin's conjecture (Ershov independent). Clear technique transfer.

events.name: Von Neumann algebras
events.summary: Weakly closed self-adjoint operator algebras on Hilbert space became a theory with Murray's classification of factors.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Algebra der Funktionaloperatoren (Math. Ann. 1930)
Murray-von Neumann, On rings of operators (Ann. Math. 1936)
events.verifierNotes: Murray-von Neumann Ann. Math. 1936 confirmed. Title of the 1930 paper is 'Zur Algebra der Funktionaloperationen und Theorie der normalen Operatoren'. Methodological date in scope.

events.name: Algebraic coding theory
events.summary: Error-correcting codes were built from algebra over finite fields.
keyWorks: Hamming, Error detecting and error correcting codes (1950)
events.verifierNotes: Hamming, BSTJ 1950 confirmed; Golay 1949; Reed-Solomon and BCH 1959-60.

events.name: Ito calculus
events.summary: Stochastic integrals gave calculus for Brownian paths.
keyWorks: Ito, Stochastic integral (1944)
events.verifierNotes: Ito, 'Stochastic integral', Proc. Imp. Acad. Tokyo 20 (1944) 519-524 confirmed via Project Euclid. Ito's formula is 1951 (Nagoya Math. J.).

events.name: Statistical decision theory
events.summary: Estimation and testing recast as games.
keyWorks: Wald, Statistical Decision Functions (1950)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Wald Ann. Math. Stat. 1939 and the 1950 book verified.

events.name: Goedel incompleteness
events.summary: Coding of syntax by numbers was used to show that consistent arithmetical systems have unprovable true statements.
keyWorks: Goedel, Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze der Principia Mathematica (1931)
events.verifierNotes: Goedel, Monatsh. Math. Phys. 38 (1931) confirmed (DOI 10.1007/BF01700692).

events.name: Four colour theorem computer proof
events.summary: Discharging plus exhaustive machine checks prove the theorem.
keyWorks: Appel, Haken, 1976-77
events.verifierNotes: Appel-Haken, Illinois J. Math. 1977, Parts I-II, confirmed (1976 announcement). Birth of computer-assisted proof.

events.name: Floer homology
events.summary: Infinite-dimensional Morse theory proved Arnold's conjecture.
keyWorks: Floer, Morse theory for Lagrangian intersections (1988)
events.verifierNotes: J. Diff. Geom. 28 (1988) confirmed.

events.name: Algebraic topology: Betti numbers to homology groups
events.summary: Numerical invariants (Betti numbers) of manifolds from the study of integrals and differential equations are replaced by groups, so algebra becomes the language of topology.
keyWorks: H. Poincare, Analysis situs, J. Ecole Polytech. 1 (1895)
H. Poincare, Complement a l'Analysis situs, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 13 (1899)
P. Alexandroff and H. Hopf, Topologie I (1935)

events.name: Functional analysis
events.summary: Integral equations and the calculus of variations are treated as linear algebra in infinite-dimensional normed spaces with topological structure.
keyWorks: D. Hilbert, Grundzuge einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen (1912; papers 1904-10)
M. Frechet, Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 22 (1906)
F. Riesz, Sur les operations fonctionnelles lineaires, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 149 (1909)
S. Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires (1932)

events.name: Group representations enter quantum mechanics
events.summary: Symmetry groups of atoms and spectra are analysed by decomposing the state space into irreducible representations, which also drives the general theory.
keyWorks: F. Peter and H. Weyl, Die Vollstandigkeit der primitiven Darstellungen einer geschlossenen kontinuierlichen Gruppe, Math. Ann. 97 (1927)
H. Weyl, Gruppentheorie und Quantenmechanik (1928)
E. Wigner, Gruppentheorie und ihre Anwendung auf die Quantenmechanik der Atomspektren (1931)

events.name: Weil's dictionary: number fields, function fields, Riemann surfaces
events.summary: A three-way analogy between number fields, function fields over finite fields and compact Riemann surfaces transfers statements and methods between arithmetic and geometry.
keyWorks: R. Dedekind and H. Weber, Theorie der algebraischen Functionen einer Veranderlichen, J. reine angew. Math. 92 (1882)
A. Weil, letter to Simone Weil (March 1940, written from Bonne-Nouvelle prison, Rouen), in Oeuvres scientifiques / Collected Papers, vol. I (1979)

events.name: Unipotent flows and the Oppenheim conjecture
events.summary: Values of indefinite quadratic forms at integer points are controlled by showing orbits of unipotent subgroups on homogeneous spaces are well-behaved.
keyWorks: G. A. Margulis, Indefinite quadratic forms and unipotent flows on homogeneous spaces, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I 304 (1987)
M. Ratner, On Raghunathan's measure conjecture, Ann. of Math. 134 (1991)

events.name: Topology proves Kneser's conjecture
events.summary: The chromatic number of Kneser graphs is bounded below via the Borsuk-Ulam theorem applied to a topological space built from the graph.

I. Barany, A short proof of Kneser's conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 25 (1978)

events.name: Random matrix statistics and the zeros of zeta
events.summary: The pair correlation of zeta zeros matches that of eigenvalues of random unitary matrices, suggesting a spectral interpretation of the zeros.
keyWorks: H. L. Montgomery, The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 24 (1973)
A. M. Odlyzko, On the distribution of spacings between zeros of the zeta function, Math. Comp. 48 (1987)
N. M. Katz and P. Sarnak, Random Matrices, Frobenius Eigenvalues, and Monodromy (1999)

events.name: Two-dimensional gravity and the moduli space of curves
events.summary: A prediction of topological gravity about intersection numbers on moduli spaces of curves is proved by combinatorial (ribbon graph) and hyperbolic-geometric routes.

events.name: Perelman's proof of the Poincare conjecture
events.summary: Ricci flow with surgery, controlled by an entropy functional and Alexandrov-space compactness, classifies three-manifolds and gives the Poincare and geometrisation conjectures.

events.name: Erdos discrepancy problem
events.summary: A combinatorial discrepancy question is reduced to correlations of multiplicative functions, then settled with entropy-decrement and short-interval results from analytic number theory.

T. Tao, The Erdos discrepancy problem, Discrete Anal. 2016:1
K. Matomaki and M. Radziwill, Multiplicative functions in short intervals, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016)

events.name: Computer science separates from mathematics
events.summary: Computability, switching theory and programming grow into a discipline with its own departments, journals and questions (complexity, algorithms) while keeping heavy mathematical exchange.

D. E. Knuth, Computer science and its relation to mathematics, Amer. Math. Monthly 81 (1974)

events.name: Function-field Langlands: Drinfeld and Lafforgue
events.summary: Moduli of Drinfeld modules and shtukas, objects of algebraic geometry over finite fields, are used to prove the Langlands correspondence for function fields.

events.name: Geometric Langlands and its physics
events.summary: The arithmetic correspondence is reformulated for curves over the complex numbers with sheaves in place of functions, and electric-magnetic duality in gauge theory is identified as its physical origin.

events.name: Hardy-Littlewood circle method
events.summary: Contour integration of generating functions and exponential sums are used to count representations of integers (partitions, sums of primes), the method behind later Fourier-analytic density arguments.

events.name: Brownian motion: from physics and finance to measure on path space
events.summary: A random motion modelled by physicists and by Bachelier is given a rigorous measure on continuous paths, which then solves boundary value problems for harmonic functions.

events.name: Computers enter proof: four colour theorem and the Kepler conjecture
events.summary: Exhaustive case analysis by computer is accepted as proof in graph theory, and later whole proofs are re-verified in proof assistants.

events.name: Boolean algebra: logic as algebra, then topology (Boole to Stone)
events.summary: Propositional logic is treated as an algebra, and Stone's theorem gives a topological dictionary for it, anticipating duality methods in logic and model theory.

events.name: Viscosity solutions: control theory meets PDE
events.summary: Dynamic-programming value functions, merely continuous, are given a rigorous notion of solution for fully nonlinear first and second order PDE.

events.name: Landau damping: plasma physics to nonlinear PDE
events.summary: A prediction of plasma physics from 1946 is proved for the nonlinear Vlasov equation in Gevrey regularity, using analytic norms and a new treatment of echoes.

events.name: Perfectoid spaces and tilting
events.summary: Characteristic p and characteristic 0 p-adic fields are related by an equivalence of Galois groups extended to geometry, moving results from one side to the other.

events.name: Shannon capacity of graphs and the Lovasz theta function
events.summary: A coding-theory quantity for graphs is bounded by a semidefinite programme, giving the theta function and its exact polynomial-time computation for perfect graphs.
keyWorks: L. Lovasz, On the Shannon capacity of a graph, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 25 (1979) 1-7

events.name: Concentration of measure
events.summary: Isoperimetric inequalities in high dimension give sharp deviation bounds for Lipschitz functions, used for Banach space geometry and probability in product spaces.

events.name: Spin glasses: the Parisi formula
events.summary: A replica-symmetry-breaking prediction for the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model is proved by interpolation arguments and ultrametricity.

events.name: Buildings: geometry of algebraic groups
events.summary: Simplicial complexes attached to groups of Lie type encode their parabolic subgroups, giving a geometric language for finite simple groups and p-adic groups.
keyWorks: J. Tits, Buildings of Spherical Type and Finite BN-Pairs, Lecture Notes in Math. 386 (1974)

events.name: Rigid analytic spaces
events.summary: Complex-analytic ideas (coherent sheaves, analytic continuation) are made to work over complete non-archimedean fields, giving p-adic uniformisation of elliptic curves.

events.name: The large sieve: harmonic analysis in analytic number theory
events.summary: Duality for trigonometric polynomials gives inequalities on sums over characters, producing the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions.

events.name: Real-variable methods in complex analysis (Hardy spaces)
events.summary: Real-variable characterisations of Hardy spaces and the duality of H^1 and BMO replace complex-variable methods in harmonic analysis.

events.summary: Hodge theory (harmonic forms) is applied to compact Kahler manifolds to prove vanishing theorems and characterise projective varieties.

events.name: Covering surfaces and value distribution (Ahlfors)

events.summary: Variational principles for rare events of Markov processes, modelled on free energy computations, become a general theory of large deviations.

events.name: Selberg trace formula and automorphic representations

events.name: Kleene theorem on regular events

events.name: Subjective and Bayesian foundations
events.summary: De Finetti and Ramsey ground probability on coherent betting; Savage extends it.

Savage, Foundations of Statistics, 1954
