events.name: Twistor theory
events.summary: Penrose encodes spacetime fields as complex geometry.
keyWorks: Penrose, Twistor algebra, 1967
events.verifierNotes: Penrose, J. Math. Phys. 8 (1967) confirmed. Methodological uptake Ward 1977, Atiyah-Ward 1977.

events.name: Rota combinatorial theory
events.summary: Moebius functions of posets unified inversion.
keyWorks: Rota, On the foundations of combinatorial theory I (1964)
events.verifierNotes: Rota, Z. Wahrsch. 2 (1964) confirmed.

events.name: Wiener-style harmonic analysis on groups
events.summary: Pontryagin duality and Plancherel on locally compact groups.

events.summary: Sato defines hyperfunctions as boundary values of holomorphic functions and develops microlocal methods.

events.name: Matroid theory and combinatorial geometry
events.summary: Whitney's abstraction of dependence unites linear algebra and graphs.

events.name: Conformal field theory

keyWorks: BPZ, Infinite conformal symmetry, 1984
events.verifierNotes: BPZ Nucl. Phys. B 241 (1984) confirmed. Physics paper; counts only via its uptake in representation theory (Borcherds 1986, FLM). Overlaps WB64.

events.name: Kolmogorov diffusion theory and PDE
events.summary: Continuous-time Markov processes were linked to parabolic equations, founding diffusion theory.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, Ueber die analytischen Methoden in der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung (Math. Ann. 1931)
events.verifierNotes: Math. Ann. 104 (1931) confirmed. PDE into probability founds continuous Markov process theory.

events.name: Hodge theory of harmonic integrals
events.summary: Harmonic forms represent cohomology on Kaehler manifolds.
keyWorks: Hodge, Theory and Applications of Harmonic Integrals (1941)
events.verifierNotes: Hodge's harmonic-integral papers 1931-36 precede the 1941 book (confirmed Open Library).

events.name: Shannon: communication theory of secrecy
events.summary: Information-theoretic concepts were used to define and bound secrecy of ciphers.
keyWorks: Shannon, Communication theory of secrecy systems (BSTJ 1949)
events.verifierNotes: Classified 1945 report precedes BSTJ 28 (1949), confirmed.

events.name: Combinatorial game theory
events.summary: Games assigned number values.
keyWorks: Conway, On Numbers and Games (1976)
events.verifierNotes: ONAG 1976 confirmed (Open Library). Sprague-Grundy 1935/39 is the root; field consolidated with Winning Ways 1982. 'game theory' here means combinatorial, not von Neumann games.

events.name: Weil: integration on topological groups, harmonic analysis
events.summary: Haar measure and Pontryagin duality were systematised in a general setting.
keyWorks: Weil, L'integration dans les groupes topologiques (1940)
events.verifierNotes: Hermann 1940 confirmed (Open Library). Builds on Haar 1933 and Pontryagin duality 1934; fusion fits better than reification.

events.name: Kripke semantics
events.summary: Relational models gave completeness theorems for modal logics.
keyWorks: Kripke, Semantical analysis of modal logic I (1963)
events.verifierNotes: Z. Math. Logik 1963 confirmed; Kripke JSL 1959 completeness theorem first. Precursors Jonsson-Tarski 1951, Kanger, Hintikka.

events.name: Computer algebra and Groebner bases
events.summary: Groebner bases and CAD give algorithms for polynomial systems.
keyWorks: Buchberger, 1965 thesis
Collins, CAD, 1975
events.verifierNotes: Buchberger 1965 thesis confirmed (Open Library) and 1985 survey (Crossref). Hironaka 1964 standard bases parallel. Collins CAD 1975 is a separate real-algebraic event; drop from this record.

events.name: Random graphs
events.summary: Graphs chosen at random were studied for thresholds of properties.
keyWorks: Erdos-Renyi, On random graphs I (1959)
Erdos-Renyi, On the evolution of random graphs (1960)
events.verifierNotes: Erdos-Renyi, Publ. Math. Inst. Hung. Acad. Sci. 5 (1960) 17-61 confirmed (zbMATH via web). 1959 Publ. Math. Debrecen paper not separately checked.

events.name: Algebraic K-theory
events.summary: K-groups of rings were defined and linked to topology via Quillen's higher K-theory.
keyWorks: Milnor, Introduction to Algebraic K-Theory (1971)
events.verifierNotes: Milnor's book is Annals Studies 72, 1971 (Crossref lists 1972). Key dates: Bass-Schanuel 1962, Bass K1 1964-68, Milnor K2 1970, Quillen higher K 1972-73.

events.name: Intersection cohomology
events.summary: Goresky and MacPherson extend Poincare duality to singular spaces.
keyWorks: Goresky, MacPherson, Intersection homology theory, 1980
events.verifierNotes: Topology 1980 confirmed. BBD 1982 and the Kazhdan-Lusztig proofs 1981 extend the fusion into representation theory.

events.name: Tarski truth definition and model theory
events.summary: A semantic definition of truth in formal languages gave the basis for the study of models of theories.
keyWorks: Tarski, Der Wahrheitsbegriff in den formalisierten Sprachen (1933)
events.verifierNotes: German version 1935 confirmed (Open Library); Polish original 1933. Tarski's 1954-55 'Contributions to the theory of models' gives the name.

events.name: Ramsey theory and Hales-Jewett
events.summary: Ramsey's partition theorem is generalised to structured colourings.
keyWorks: Ramsey, On a problem of formal logic, 1930
Hales, Jewett, Regularity and positional games, 1963
events.verifierNotes: Hales-Jewett, Trans. AMS 1963 confirmed. Ramsey 1930 lemma, from a decision problem in logic, was reused by Erdos-Szekeres 1935; field consolidated with Graham-Rothschild 1971.

events.name: Deligne proof of Weil conjectures
events.summary: Etale cohomology plus Lefschetz pencils and Rankin methods proved the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields.
keyWorks: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil I (Publ. IHES 1974)
events.verifierNotes: Publ. IHES 43 (1974) confirmed. Rankin's squaring trick from modular forms is the real bridge; overlaps WB44.

events.name: Operator K-theory and KK-theory
events.summary: Kasparov links K-homology to elliptic operators.
keyWorks: Kasparov, The operator K-functor and extensions of C*-algebras, 1980
events.verifierNotes: Kasparov, Izv. 1980 (English 1981) confirmed. Brown-Douglas-Fillmore 1973/77 is the conceptual start.

events.name: Kodaira-Spencer deformation theory
events.summary: Deformations of complex structures were studied by cohomology.
keyWorks: Kodaira-Spencer (1958)
events.verifierNotes: Annals 1958 (parts I-II; III 1960) confirmed. Birth of deformation theory of complex structures.

events.name: Nonabelian Hodge, Hodge theory of Deligne
events.summary: Deligne uses weights to prove the Weil conjectures.
keyWorks: Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, 1971
events.verifierNotes: Publ. IHES 1971 confirmed. Mislabelled: Hodge II is mixed Hodge theory, carrying Grothendieck's weight philosophy from l-adic to complex; 'nonabelian Hodge' (Hitchin-Simpson-Corlette 1987-92) is a different event.

events.name: Automata and formal verification
events.summary: Floyd and Hoare apply logic to program correctness.
keyWorks: Hoare, An axiomatic basis for computer programming, 1969
events.verifierNotes: Hoare, CACM 12 (1969) confirmed (Crossref reprint records); Floyd 1967. It is a transfer from logic, not a split.

events.name: Bott periodicity
events.summary: Loop spaces of classical groups were shown periodic.
keyWorks: Bott, The stable homotopy of the classical groups (1959)
events.verifierNotes: PNAS 1957 and Annals 1959 confirmed.

events.name: Nash embedding theorem
events.summary: A new implicit function technique solved the isometric embedding problem for Riemannian manifolds.
keyWorks: Nash, C1 isometric imbeddings (Ann. Math. 1954)
Nash, The imbedding problem for Riemannian manifolds (1956)
events.verifierNotes: Annals 1954 and 1956 confirmed. The 1956 hard implicit-function (Nash-Moser) method is the transferable tool.

events.name: Serre: spectral sequences and homotopy groups
events.summary: Leray's spectral sequence applied to fibrations gave homotopy results for spheres.
keyWorks: Serre, Homologie singuliere des espaces fibres (Ann. Math. 1951)
events.verifierNotes: Annals 1951 confirmed.

events.name: Algebraic combinatorics / Young tableaux
events.summary: Symmetric functions and tableaux are linked to representations (Schensted, Stanley).
keyWorks: Schensted, 1961
Stanley, 1971
events.verifierNotes: Schensted 1961 (Canad. J. Math.) confirmed; Stanley 1971 not checked. Algebraic combinatorics forms in the 1970s (Knuth 1970 RSK, Stanley) by joining symmetric functions/representations with enumeration; Schensted is a combinatorial precursor.

events.name: Kantorovich linear programming
events.summary: Production-planning problems were posed as linear optimisation with multipliers, with solution methods.
keyWorks: Kantorovich, Mathematical Methods of Organizing and Planning Production (1939)
events.verifierNotes: Kantorovich 1939 confirmed (English translation in Management Science 1960). Birth of linear programming from planning problems.

events.name: MCMC revival of Bayesian statistics
events.summary: Metropolis-type samplers, via Gibbs sampling, make posterior computation feasible.
keyWorks: Metropolis et al., 1953
Geman, Geman, Stochastic relaxation, Gibbs distributions, 1984
Gelfand, Smith, 1990
events.verifierNotes: Geman and Geman, IEEE PAMI 1984 confirmed. A statistical-physics sampler moved into Bayesian computation; methodological 1984-1990 (Gelfand-Smith 1990).

events.name: Cellular automata and self-reproducing machines
events.summary: Von Neumann and Ulam model self-reproduction by lattice automata.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Theory of Self-Reproducing Automata (ed. Burks), 1966
events.verifierNotes: von Neumann/Burks 1966 confirmed (Math. Comp. review 1967). The conceptual work dates from about 1948-52; it is a real field birth.

events.name: Computational geometry
events.summary: Shamos names the field and gives algorithms for geometric problems.
keyWorks: Shamos, Hoey, Closest-point problems, 1975
events.verifierNotes: Shamos-Hoey, FOCS 1975 confirmed. Shamos's 1978 thesis names the field.

events.name: Pontryagin maximum principle
events.summary: Necessary conditions for optimal control extended variational calculus.
keyWorks: Pontryagin et al., Mathematical Theory of Optimal Processes (1962)
events.verifierNotes: Pontryagin et al. book (Russian 1961, English 1962) confirmed. Birth of optimal control, alongside Bellman's dynamic programming (1957).

events.name: Kantorovich functional analysis for numerical methods
events.summary: Ordered vector spaces and normed spaces were applied to approximation and equation solving.
keyWorks: Kantorovich, On one class of functional equations (1936)
Kantorovich-Akilov, Functional Analysis in Normed Spaces (1959)
events.verifierNotes: The bridge paper is Kantorovich, 'Functional analysis and applied mathematics', Uspekhi 1948 (not found in Crossref); the 1936 date is doubtful. Kantorovich-Akilov book confirmed (later edition). Functional analysis transferred into numerical analysis.

events.name: Feynman-Kac formula
events.summary: Path integrals matched with expectations over Brownian paths.
keyWorks: Kac, On distributions of certain Wiener functionals (1949)
events.verifierNotes: Kac, Trans. AMS 1949 confirmed. Feynman 1948 path integral plus Wiener measure gives the bridge between probability and PDE.

events.name: Heat equation proof of index theorem
events.summary: Heat kernels give local proofs of the index formula.
keyWorks: Atiyah, Bott, Patodi, 1973
Getzler, 1983
events.verifierNotes: Atiyah-Bott-Patodi, Invent. Math. 1973 confirmed (reprints). Getzler 1983 adds supersymmetric methods.

events.name: Ribet and modularity
events.summary: Ribet shows Frey curve would contradict modularity.
keyWorks: Ribet, On modular representations of Gal arising from modular forms, 1990
events.verifierNotes: Ribet, Invent. Math. 1990 confirmed (result 1986). Frey 1985, Serre and Ribet tie FLT to modularity through Galois representations; a technique transfer more than a dictionary.

events.name: Vertex operator algebras
events.summary: Borcherds and FLM axiomatise vertex operators to build the moonshine module.
keyWorks: Borcherds, Vertex algebras, Kac-Moody algebras, and the Monster, 1986
events.verifierNotes: Borcherds, PNAS 1986 confirmed; Frenkel-Lepowsky-Meurman 1988.

events.name: Mathematical economics via fixed points
events.summary: Arrow-Debreu equilibrium existence by fixed-point theorem.
keyWorks: Arrow, Debreu, 1954
events.verifierNotes: Arrow-Debreu, Econometrica 1954 confirmed. Precursors von Neumann 1937 and Wald 1936 also used fixed-point methods in economics.

events.name: Blum-Shub-Smale real computation
events.summary: A machine model over the reals combined Turing computability with numerical analysis.
keyWorks: Blum-Shub-Smale, On a theory of computation over the real numbers (Bull. AMS 1989)
events.verifierNotes: Blum-Shub-Smale, Bull. AMS 1989 confirmed.

events.name: Surgery theory
events.summary: Surgery classifies high-dimensional manifolds via algebraic obstruction groups.
keyWorks: Kervaire, Milnor, 1963
Browder, Novikov, Wall, Surgery on Compact Manifolds, 1970
events.verifierNotes: Kervaire-Milnor, Annals 1963 confirmed. Browder 1962, Novikov 1962-65 and Wall 1970 follow.

events.name: Network flows and combinatorial optimisation
events.summary: Max-flow min-cut ties graph theory to LP duality (Ford-Fulkerson, Edmonds).
keyWorks: Ford, Fulkerson, Flows in Networks, 1962
Edmonds, 1965
events.verifierNotes: Real; Ford-Fulkerson Canad. J. Math. 1956 and Edmonds 'Paths, trees, and flowers' 1965 verified (RAND memo 1954).

events.name: Chern: intrinsic Gauss-Bonnet and characteristic classes
events.summary: Curvature forms gave topological invariants.
keyWorks: Chern, A simple intrinsic proof of Gauss-Bonnet (1944)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Chern Annals 1944 verified; curvature-to-topology bridge leading to Chern classes (1946). Overlaps WB121.

events.name: Several complex variables via PDE
events.summary: L2 estimates for the d-bar equation solved problems about pseudoconvex domains.
keyWorks: Hoermander, L2 estimates and existence theorems for the d-bar operator (Acta 1965)
Hoermander, Introduction to Complex Analysis in Several Variables (1966)
events.verifierNotes: Real but borderline: Hilbert-space L2 methods (Morrey 1958, Kohn 1963, Hormander Acta 1965 verified) settled Levi problem-type questions.

events.name: Lie algebra cohomology
events.summary: Cohomology of compact Lie groups was computed algebraically via Lie algebras.
keyWorks: Chevalley-Eilenberg, Cohomology theory of Lie groups and Lie algebras (1948)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Chevalley-Eilenberg Trans. AMS 1948 verified; topology to algebra.

events.name: Hirzebruch Riemann-Roch
events.summary: Characteristic classes expressed Euler characteristic of bundles.
keyWorks: Hirzebruch, Neue topologische Methoden in der algebraischen Geometrie (1956)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Hirzebruch book 1956 verified (announced 1954).

events.name: Feigenbaum universality
events.summary: Renormalisation explains universal constants in the period-doubling route.
keyWorks: Feigenbaum, Quantitative universality for a class of nonlinear transformations, 1978
Coullet, Tresser, 1978
events.verifierNotes: Real; physics renormalisation imported into 1-d dynamics. Feigenbaum J. Stat. Phys. 1978 verified.

events.name: Operations research
events.summary: Wartime scientific analysis of radar and convoys becomes a quantitative decision discipline.
keyWorks: Blackett, reports of the Circus group, 1941
events.verifierNotes: Real import; Blackett's 1941 'circus' memos are unpublished. Crossref has Blackett 'Operational research' (1950); collected in Studies of War (1962).

events.name: Global analysis and mathematical economics
events.summary: Topological and dynamical methods were applied to equilibrium existence and price adjustment.
keyWorks: Smale, Global analysis and economics (Handbook of Math Economics 1981)
events.verifierNotes: Borderline but real; Debreu 1970 and Smale's series in J. Math. Econ. (1974-76 verified). Handbook chapter 1981 is a later survey.

events.name: Abelian categories and derived functors (Tohoku)
events.summary: A common axiomatic framework unified derived functors for modules and sheaves.
keyWorks: Grothendieck, Sur quelques points d'algebre homologique (Tohoku 1957)
events.verifierNotes: Real reification; Tohoku 1957 I/II verified (Buchsbaum 1955 had exact categories).

events.name: Hilbert space foundations of quantum mechanics
events.summary: Quantum mechanics was given a rigorous Hilbert space and spectral theorem basis.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik (1932)
events.verifierNotes: Real; methodological date 1932 is in scope. The book is verified via a Springer reprint record.

events.name: Gromov polynomial growth via geometry
events.summary: Large-scale geometry shows polynomial growth implies virtual nilpotence.
keyWorks: Gromov, Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps, 1981
events.verifierNotes: Real; Gromov Publ. IHES 1981 verified.

events.name: Iwasawa theory
events.summary: Class groups in infinite towers are studied with module theory over Iwasawa algebras.
keyWorks: Iwasawa, On the theory of cyclotomic fields, 1959
events.verifierNotes: Real; modelled on Weil's function-field analogy. The 1959 papers are 'On Gamma-extensions' (Bull. AMS) and 'Gamma-finite modules' (Annals), both verified. 'On the theory of cyclotomic fields' is Annals 1964.

events.name: Serre GAGA
events.summary: Analytic and algebraic coherent sheaf cohomology on projective varieties were shown to agree.
keyWorks: Serre, Geometrie algebrique et geometrie analytique (1956)
events.verifierNotes: Real; Serre, Ann. Inst. Fourier 1956 verified.

events.name: Sobolev generalised solutions
events.summary: Weak derivatives and function spaces were introduced to treat generalised solutions of wave and elliptic equations.
keyWorks: Sobolev, Methode nouvelle a resoudre le probleme de Cauchy (1936)
events.verifierNotes: Real (Sobolev 1935-38). Crossref and Open Library did not find the 1936 Mat. Sb. paper; only the later monograph (English 1963) was found.

events.name: Tate's thesis and adelic harmonic analysis
events.summary: Fourier analysis on idele groups gave a new proof of functional equations for Hecke L-functions.
keyWorks: Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta functions (1950)
events.verifierNotes: Real; the 1950 Princeton thesis was published in Cassels-Frohlich, Algebraic Number Theory (1967), confirmed via Open Library.

events.name: Bass-Serre theory
events.summary: Group actions on trees decompose groups as amalgams and HNN extensions.
keyWorks: Serre, Arbres, amalgames, SL2, 1977
events.verifierNotes: Real; Serre's 1968-69 course, Asterisque 46 (1977). The English 'Trees' (1980) is verified.

events.name: Random matrices and zeta zeros
events.summary: Rudnick-Sarnak and Keating-Snaith matched statistics of zeta zeros to random matrix moments.
keyWorks: Keating, Snaith, Random matrix theory and zeta(1/2+it), CMP 2000
events.verifierNotes: Keating-Snaith CMP 214 (2000); Katz-Sarnak 1999. Dictionary born 1973 (Montgomery-Dyson); in scope only by its methodological use for moment conjectures.

events.name: Geometric group theory
events.summary: Finitely generated groups are studied as metric spaces up to quasi-isometry, so large-scale geometry classifies algebraic properties.
keyWorks: M. Gromov, Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps, Publ. Math. IHES 53 (1981)
M. Gromov, Hyperbolic groups, in Essays in Group Theory, MSRI Publ. 8 (1987)

events.name: Noncommutative geometry
events.summary: Geometric invariants (cohomology, index theory) are extended to operator algebras viewed as spaces of noncommutative functions.
keyWorks: A. Connes, Non-commutative differential geometry, Publ. Math. IHES 62 (1985)
A. Connes, Noncommutative Geometry (1994)

events.name: Monstrous moonshine
to: finite group theory and modular forms
events.summary: Borcherds proved Conway-Norton monstrous moonshine using the Monster vertex algebra and generalised Kac-Moody algebras.
keyWorks: Borcherds, Monstrous moonshine and monstrous Lie superalgebras, Invent. 1992
Frenkel-Lepowsky-Meurman, Vertex operator algebras and the Monster, 1988
events.verifierNotes: Borcherds Invent. 109 (1992); FLM 1988. Duplicate of QC55. The 1998 institutional date (Fields Medal) is not institutional.

events.name: 2D gravity / Witten-Kontsevich
events.summary: Intersection numbers on moduli of curves were shown to be governed by KdV hierarchy via a matrix-model ribbon graph computation.
keyWorks: Witten, Two-dimensional gravity and intersection theory on moduli space, 1991
Kontsevich, Intersection theory on the moduli space of curves and the matrix Airy function, CMP 1992
events.verifierNotes: Kontsevich CMP 1992 (10.1007/bf02099526) and Witten Surveys Diff. Geom. 1990/91 confirmed; ribbon graphs and matrix Airy integrals settled the moduli-space conjecture.

events.name: Mirzakhani moduli volumes
to: intersection theory on moduli of curves
events.summary: Mirzakhani computed Weil-Petersson volumes, recovered Witten's conjecture, and established Teichmuller-dynamics rigidity (with Eskin).
keyWorks: Mirzakhani, Simple geodesics and Weil-Petersson volumes, Invent. 2007
Eskin-Mirzakhani, Invariant and stationary measures for the SL(2,R) action on moduli space, Publ.IHES 2018
events.verifierNotes: Mirzakhani Invent. 167 (2007) and JAMS 20 (2007), a new proof of Witten-Kontsevich. Eskin-Mirzakhani (arXiv 1302.3320) is a separate dynamics event and should be split.

events.name: Mirror symmetry
events.summary: Physicists' mirror computation of rational curve counts on the quintic threefold launched a mathematical programme of enumerative predictions and proofs.
keyWorks: Candelas-de la Ossa-Green-Parkes, A pair of Calabi-Yau manifolds as an exactly soluble superconformal theory, Nucl.Phys.B 1991
Givental, Equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants, IMRN 1996
Lian-Liu-Yau, Mirror principle I, 1997
events.verifierNotes: Candelas-de la Ossa-Green-Parkes Nucl. Phys. B 1991 checked; proved by Givental 1996 and Lian-Liu-Yau 1997.

events.name: Homological mirror symmetry
events.summary: Kontsevich conjectured an equivalence between Fukaya and derived categories of mirror varieties.
keyWorks: Kontsevich, Homological algebra of mirror symmetry, ICM 1994, arXiv:alg-geom/9411018
events.verifierNotes: Kontsevich alg-geom/9411018, ICM Zurich proc. 1995. Distinct from physical mirror symmetry (1989-91).

events.name: Modularity and FLT
events.summary: Wiles and Taylor-Wiles proved modularity of semistable elliptic curves via Hecke algebra patching, giving Fermat's Last Theorem.
keyWorks: Wiles, Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Annals 1995
Taylor, Wiles, Ring-theoretic properties of Hecke algebras, Annals 1995
events.verifierNotes: Wiles, Annals 141 (1995); Taylor-Wiles same issue. R=T patching joins deformation theory and Hecke algebras.

events.name: SLE
events.summary: Schramm introduced SLE; Lawler-Schramm-Werner identified percolation exponents.
keyWorks: Schramm, Scaling limits of loop-erased random walks, Israel J. Math. 2000, arXiv:math/9904022
events.verifierNotes: Schramm arXiv math/9904022, Israel J. Math 118 (2000).

events.name: Green-Tao
events.summary: A transference principle lets Szemeredi's theorem apply inside a pseudorandom majorant of the primes, giving arbitrarily long progressions of primes.
keyWorks: Green, Tao, The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, Annals 2008, arXiv:math/0404188
events.verifierNotes: Green-Tao Annals 2008, arXiv math/0404188 checked; ergodic-style structure theory plus Goldston-Yildirim sieve weights settle progressions in the primes.

events.name: Guth-Katz distinct distances
from: real algebraic geometry (polynomial partitioning, ruled surfaces)
events.summary: Guth and Katz used polynomial partitioning and ruled surface results to nearly solve the distinct distances problem.
keyWorks: Guth-Katz, On the Erdos distinct distances problem in the plane, Annals 2015 (arXiv:1011.4105)
events.verifierNotes: Guth-Katz arXiv 1011.4105 (Nov 2010), Annals 181 (2015). Conceptual: Dvir 2008 / Guth-Katz joints 2008 and Elekes-Sharir reduction. Duplicate of QC23; keep one.

events.name: Cap set
events.summary: Croot-Lev-Pach and Ellenberg-Gijswijt used a low-degree polynomial argument to bound cap sets.
keyWorks: Ellenberg, Gijswijt, On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression, Annals 2017, arXiv:1605.09223
events.verifierNotes: Ellenberg-Gijswijt Annals 2017, arXiv 1605.09223 checked; builds on Croot-Lev-Pach 2016. The tool is the linear-algebraic polynomial method, not algebraic geometry.

events.name: Additive combinatorics and expansion
events.summary: Sum-product theorems yielded spectral gaps for Cayley graphs of SL_2(F_p) and related groups.
keyWorks: Bourgain-Gamburd, Uniform expansion bounds for Cayley graphs of SL2(Fp), Annals 2008
Helfgott, Growth and generation in SL2(Z/pZ), Annals 2008
events.verifierNotes: Bourgain-Gamburd, Annals 167 (2008), and Helfgott, math/0509024, confirmed.

events.name: Perelman / Poincare
events.summary: Ricci flow with surgery, controlled by entropy monotonicity, settled Poincare and Thurston geometrization conjectures.
keyWorks: Perelman, The entropy formula for the Ricci flow, arXiv:math/0211159
Perelman, Ricci flow with surgery on three-manifolds, arXiv:math/0303109
Hamilton, Three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, JDG 1982
events.verifierNotes: Perelman arXiv math/0211159, math/0303109. Hamilton 1982 programme is the conceptual date; methodological 2002-03 in scope.

events.name: Sphere packing 8, 24
events.summary: Viazovska constructed magic functions from quasi-modular forms to prove optimality of E8 and Leech lattices.
keyWorks: Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 8, Annals 2017
Cohn-Kumar-Miller-Radchenko-Viazovska, The sphere packing problem in dimension 24, Annals 2017
events.verifierNotes: Viazovska arXiv:1603.04246 and Cohn-Kumar-Miller-Radchenko-Viazovska arXiv:1603.06518 confirmed (Annals 2017). Conceptual date: Cohn-Elkies LP bound, Annals 2003.

events.name: Optimal transport and Ricci curvature
events.summary: Lott-Villani and Sturm defined Ricci curvature bounds on metric measure spaces via optimal transport.
keyWorks: Lott, Villani, Ricci curvature for metric-measure spaces via optimal transport, Annals 2009, arXiv:math/0412127
events.verifierNotes: Lott-Villani arXiv math/0412127, Annals 169 (2009); Sturm Acta 2006; Otto-Villani 2000 precursor.

events.name: Hodge theory for matroids
events.summary: Kahler-package-type properties were proved for Chow rings of matroids, settling log-concavity conjectures and Rota's conjecture.
keyWorks: Adiprasito-Huh-Katz, Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries, Annals 2018 (arXiv:1511.02888)
Huh-Katz, Log-concavity of characteristic polynomials and the Bergman fan of matroids, Math.Ann. 2012
events.verifierNotes: AHK arXiv 1511.02888, Annals 188 (2018); Huh-Katz arXiv 1104.2519; Huh JAMS 2012.

events.name: Regularity structures
events.summary: A systematic theory of singular subcritical SPDEs such as KPZ and Phi^4_3 built via local Taylor-like expansions and renormalisation.
keyWorks: Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, Invent. 2014
Hairer, Solving the KPZ equation, Annals 2013
events.verifierNotes: Hairer Invent. 198 (2014), arXiv 1303.5113; KPZ paper Annals 178 (2013), arXiv 2011.

events.name: Rough paths
events.summary: Lyons gave a pathwise integration theory beyond bounded variation using iterated integrals.
keyWorks: Lyons, Differential equations driven by rough signals, Rev.Mat.Iberoam. 1998
events.verifierNotes: Lyons Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 1998 checked; precursor Lyons 1994 MRL. Young integration and Chen iterated integrals give a new theory.

events.name: Erdos discrepancy
events.summary: Tao used Polymath5's reduction and Fourier/entropy methods for multiplicative functions to settle the Erdos discrepancy problem; SAT solvers had done the c=2 case earlier.
keyWorks: Tao, The Erdos discrepancy problem, Discrete Analysis 2016 (arXiv:1509.05363)
Konev-Lisitsa, A SAT attack on the Erdos discrepancy conjecture, 2014
events.verifierNotes: Tao, Discrete Analysis 2016 (arXiv 1509.05363). Polymath5 2010 reduction to multiplicative functions plus Matomaki-Radziwill. Problem date 1932 is not the event date.

events.name: PFR via entropy
events.summary: Entropy methods proved a polynomial bound for small-doubling sets in F_2^n.
keyWorks: Gowers, Green, Manners, Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, arXiv:2311.05762
events.verifierNotes: GGMT arXiv 2311.05762, Annals 201 (2025); formalised in Lean. Entropy methods existed since Ruzsa/Tao c.2009, so medium.

events.name: O-minimality in diophantine geometry
events.summary: Pila-Zannier strategy uses counting rational points on definable sets.
keyWorks: Pila, Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke 2006
events.verifierNotes: Pila-Wilkie Duke 133 (2006); Pila-Zannier 2008; Pila Annals 2011; Pila-Shankar-Tsimerman full Andre-Oort 2021.

events.name: Function-field Langlands
events.summary: Compactified moduli of shtukas gave the Langlands correspondence for GL_r over function fields.
keyWorks: Lafforgue, Chtoucas de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands, Invent. 2002
events.verifierNotes: Lafforgue Invent. 2002 checked. Extends Drinfeld's 1974-87 shtuka bridge from GL2 to GLn. The bridge itself predates 1990, so this is a settlement event, not a new dictionary.

events.name: Geometric Langlands
events.summary: Langlands reformulated for curves over any field via D-modules; Kapustin-Witten tied it to S-duality; a categorical unramified case was announced proved in 2024.
keyWorks: Kapustin-Witten, Electric-magnetic duality and the geometric Langlands program, 2007 (hep-th/0604151)
Gaitsgory-Raskin et al., proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture, 2024
events.verifierNotes: Kapustin-Witten hep-th/0604151, CNTP 1 (2007); Gaitsgory-Raskin et al. proof arXiv 2405.03599 etc. (2024, under review). The geometric Langlands dictionary itself is 1983-87 (out of scope); only the physics import is in scope.

events.name: Deformation quantization
events.summary: Every Poisson manifold admits a star-product, proved via a formality theorem for polydifferential operators.
keyWorks: Kontsevich, Deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds, Lett.Math.Phys. 2003 (q-alg/9709040)
events.verifierNotes: q-alg/9709040 (1997) confirmed; Lett. Math. Phys. 66 (2003). The formality proof already appears in the 1997 preprint, so the methodological date is 1997, not 2003.

events.name: A^1-homotopy / motivic cohomology
events.summary: Voevodsky built motivic and A^1-homotopy theories and used them to prove the Milnor conjecture on K-theory mod 2.
keyWorks: Morel-Voevodsky, A^1-homotopy theory of schemes, Publ.IHES 1999
Voevodsky, Motivic cohomology with Z/2 coefficients, Publ.IHES 2003
events.verifierNotes: Morel-Voevodsky Publ.IHES 90 (1999); Voevodsky Publ.IHES 98 (2003), Milnor conjecture preprint 1996; Fields 2002.

events.name: Bloch-Kato / norm residue
events.summary: Motivic Steenrod operations proved the norm residue isomorphism in all primes.
keyWorks: Voevodsky, On motivic cohomology with Z/l-coefficients, Annals 2011
events.verifierNotes: Voevodsky Annals 2011 checked; the method dates from the Milnor-conjecture proof (1996 preprint, 2003 Publ. IHES). The conceptual date is out of scope; the methodological date is in scope.

events.name: Landau damping
events.summary: A prediction of plasma physics from 1946 is proved for the nonlinear Vlasov equation in Gevrey regularity, using analytic norms and a new treatment of echoes.
keyWorks: C. Mouhot and C. Villani, On Landau damping, Acta Math. 207 (2011) 29-201

events.name: Bhargava arithmetic statistics
events.summary: Parametrising rings and orbits of prehomogeneous spaces allowed counting arithmetic objects and bounding average ranks of elliptic curves.
keyWorks: Bhargava, Higher composition laws I-IV, Annals 2004-08
Bhargava-Shankar, Binary quartic forms having bounded invariants..., Annals 2015
events.verifierNotes: Bhargava-Shankar Annals 2015 (arXiv 2010) checked; parametrisation plus geometry-of-numbers counting founded modern arithmetic statistics; Davenport-Heilbronn is a pre-1990 precursor.

events.name: Perfectoid spaces
events.summary: Scholze generalised Fontaine-Wintenberger to perfectoid spaces, with a tilting equivalence between char 0 and char p.
keyWorks: Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Publ. IHES 2012, arXiv:1111.4914
events.verifierNotes: Scholze arXiv 1111.4914, Publ.IHES 116 (2012). Institutional possibly MSC2020 14G45 (unverified); the 2018 date is the Fields Medal, not institutional.

events.name: Prismatic cohomology
events.summary: A single cohomology theory was constructed that specializes to etale, de Rham and crystalline p-adic theories.
keyWorks: Bhatt-Scholze, Prisms and prismatic cohomology, Annals 2022 (arXiv:1905.08229)
events.verifierNotes: Bhatt-Scholze arXiv 1905.08229, Annals 196 (2022). Precursor Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze A_inf cohomology 2016. Unification of p-adic cohomologies; derived AG is a tool, not a source field.

events.name: Kakeya in 3D
events.summary: A volume estimate for unions of convex sets obtained from incidence geometry and multi-scale arguments settles the Kakeya set conjecture in R^3.
keyWorks: H. Wang and J. Zahl, Volume estimates for unions of convex sets, and the Kakeya set conjecture in three dimensions, arXiv:2502.17655 (2025)

events.name: Boltzmann from hard spheres
events.summary: Hilbert's sixth-problem programme of deriving kinetic equations from Newtonian particle systems is carried to long times for hard spheres.
keyWorks: Y. Deng, Z. Hani and X. Ma, Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard sphere dynamics, arXiv:2408.07818 (2024)

events.name: Cobordism hypothesis
events.summary: Fully extended TQFTs were classified by fully dualizable objects of a symmetric monoidal infinity-category.
keyWorks: Baez-Dolan, Higher-dimensional algebra and TQFT, J.Math.Phys. 1995
Lurie, On the classification of topological field theories, 2009 (arXiv:0905.0465)
events.verifierNotes: Baez-Dolan J.Math.Phys 36 (1995, q-alg/9503002); Lurie arXiv 0905.0465 is a proof sketch; full details debated. Duplicate of QC41.

events.name: Higher-order Fourier analysis
events.summary: Gowers uniformity norms, matched with Host-Kra ergodic seminorms, produced a nonabelian Fourier theory for polynomial patterns.
keyWorks: Gowers, A new proof of Szemeredi's theorem, GAFA 2001
Host, Kra, Nonconventional ergodic averages and nilmanifolds, Annals 2005
events.verifierNotes: Gowers GAFA 8 (1998) and 11 (2001); Host-Kra Annals 2005; Green-Tao-Ziegler inverse theorem Annals 2012; Tao book 2012.

events.name: Smirnov conformal invariance
events.summary: Smirnov proved conformal invariance of critical Ising and percolation using discrete holomorphicity.
keyWorks: Smirnov, Conformal invariance in random cluster models I, Annals 2010, arXiv:0708.0039
events.verifierNotes: Smirnov arXiv 0708.0039, Annals 172 (2010); discrete holomorphicity first used for percolation 2001 (Cardy formula).

events.name: Umbral / Mathieu moonshine
events.summary: Eguchi-Ooguri-Tachikawa observed M24 in K3 elliptic genus, leading to umbral moonshine.
keyWorks: Eguchi, Ooguri, Tachikawa, Notes on the K3 surface and Mathieu group M24, arXiv:1004.0956
events.verifierNotes: Eguchi-Ooguri-Tachikawa arXiv 1004.0956, Exp. Math 2011; Cheng-Duncan-Harvey umbral 2012; Gannon proved Mathieu moonshine 2016, Duncan-Griffin-Ono umbral 2015.

events.name: Local Langlands for GL_n
to: representation theory of p-adic groups (local Langlands)
events.summary: Harris-Taylor and Henniart proved the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n through the cohomology of Shimura varieties.
keyWorks: Harris-Taylor, The geometry and cohomology of some simple Shimura varieties, Princeton 2001
Henniart, Une preuve simple des conjectures de Langlands pour GL(n), Invent. 2000
events.verifierNotes: Harris-Taylor Annals of Math Studies 151 (2001); Henniart Invent. 139 (2000). Global geometry used to settle a local problem.

events.name: Sensitivity conjecture
events.summary: Huang's signed hypercube adjacency matrix and eigenvalue interlacing settled the sensitivity conjecture in a page.
keyWorks: Huang, Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture, Annals 2019 (arXiv:1907.00847)
events.verifierNotes: Huang Annals 190 (2019), arXiv 1907.00847. Gotsman-Linial 1992 reduction is the bridge; conjecture Nisan-Szegedy 1992/1994.

events.name: Additive combinatorics as a field
events.summary: Structure-versus-randomness for sets with small sumset consolidated into a discipline with a dedicated textbook.
keyWorks: Tao-Vu, Additive Combinatorics, CUP 2006
Bourgain-Katz-Tao, A sum-product estimate in finite fields, GAFA 2004
events.verifierNotes: BKT GAFA 2004 checked; Gowers 1998/2001 is the conceptual trigger, and the Tao-Vu 2006 textbook is institutional.

events.name: Ramanujan graphs / interlacing
events.summary: Marcus, Spielman and Srivastava proved existence of bipartite Ramanujan graphs of all degrees via interlacing polynomials, also solving Kadison-Singer.
keyWorks: Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava, Interlacing families I, Annals 2015
Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava, Interlacing families II: Kadison-Singer, Annals 2015
events.verifierNotes: MSS Annals 2015 (FOCS 2013) checked; the same method settled Kadison-Singer, so operator algebras should be added as a target.

events.name: PCP theorem
events.summary: Probabilistically checkable proofs link NP verification with low-degree testing and imply hardness of approximation.
keyWorks: Arora-Lund-Motwani-Sudan-Szegedy, Proof verification and hardness of approximation problems, JACM 1998
Arora-Safra, Probabilistic checking of proofs, JACM 1998
events.verifierNotes: ALMSS FOCS 1992 and JACM 1998 checked; conceptual start is FGLSS / Babai-Fortnow-Lund 1990-91. QC16 duplicates this; merge them.

events.name: Khovanov homology
events.summary: The Jones polynomial was lifted to a bigraded homology theory, starting a categorification programme.
keyWorks: Khovanov, A categorification of the Jones polynomial, Duke Math. J. 2000 (math/9908171)
events.verifierNotes: Khovanov, math/9908171 (Duke 2000), confirmed. Duplicate of QC39.

events.name: Topological data analysis
events.summary: Persistent homology gave a computable, stable topological summary of point clouds, with a structure theorem from commutative algebra.
keyWorks: Edelsbrunner-Letscher-Zomorodian, Topological persistence and simplification, DCG 2002
Zomorodian-Carlsson, Computing persistent homology, DCG 2005
Carlsson, Topology and data, BAMS 2009
events.verifierNotes: ELZ FOCS 2000 / DCG 2002 checked. Frosini's size functions (1990-92) are the conceptual start; Zomorodian-Carlsson 2005 and Carlsson BAMS 2009 consolidate.

events.name: Unique games conjecture
events.summary: A conjecture about label cover instances yields tight hardness for many problems via Fourier-analytic dictatorship tests and SDP integrality gaps.
keyWorks: Khot, On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games, STOC 2002
Khot-Kindler-Mossel-O'Donnell, Optimal inapproximability results for MAX-CUT, FOCS 2004
events.verifierNotes: Khot STOC/CCC 2002 checked; KKMO FOCS 2004 (SICOMP 2007) and Raghavendra 2008 tie SDP and Fourier analysis to optimal hardness. The conjecture is still open, but the research area is real.

events.name: Homotopy type theory
events.summary: Identity types read as paths led Voevodsky to univalence and a synthetic homotopy theory in type theory.
keyWorks: Voevodsky, Univalent foundations, 2010
Univalent Foundations Program, Homotopy Type Theory, 2013
events.verifierNotes: HoTT book arXiv 1308.0729 (2013) checked. Awodey-Warren 2007/09 and Voevodsky 2006-09 are the conceptual start.

events.name: Cluster algebras
events.summary: Fomin and Zelevinsky introduced mutation-based algebras unifying total positivity and canonical bases.
keyWorks: Fomin-Zelevinsky, Cluster algebras I, JAMS 2002
events.verifierNotes: Fomin-Zelevinsky JAMS 2002 (online Dec 2001) checked.

events.name: Gromov-Witten / quantum cohomology
events.summary: Physical topological sigma models gave counts of curves; Ruan-Tian and Kontsevich-Manin made them rigorous.
keyWorks: Kontsevich, Manin, Gromov-Witten classes, quantum cohomology, CMP 1994, arXiv:hep-th/9402147
events.verifierNotes: Kontsevich-Manin CMP 1994 checked; Witten 1988-91 and Ruan-Tian 1994. Overlaps WC1.

events.name: Geometric complexity theory
events.summary: Mulmuley-Sohoni proposed attacking P versus NP via orbit closures and representation theory.
keyWorks: Mulmuley, Sohoni, Geometric complexity theory I, SIAM J. Comput. 2001
events.verifierNotes: Mulmuley-Sohoni SIAM J. Comput. 2001 checked. A field was born, though its main goal is unachieved (no-occurrence obstructions fail, Burgisser-Ikenmeyer-Panova 2016).

events.name: Condensed mathematics
events.summary: Sheaves on profinite sets replace topological spaces so that topological abelian groups form an abelian category with good homological algebra.
keyWorks: Clausen-Scholze, Lectures on Condensed Mathematics, 2019
Clausen-Scholze, Condensed Mathematics and Complex Geometry, 2022
events.verifierNotes: Scholze's 2019 Bonn lectures (joint with Clausen) checked; a stable version is arXiv 2605.03658 (2026).

events.name: Compressed sensing
events.summary: Sparse signals can be recovered from few random measurements by L1 minimisation, combining random matrix theory and convex geometry.
keyWorks: Candes-Romberg-Tao, Robust uncertainty principles, IEEE Trans.Inf.Theory 2006
Donoho, Compressed sensing, IEEE Trans.Inf.Theory 2006
events.verifierNotes: CRT IEEE TIT 2006 and Donoho IEEE TIT 2006 confirmed.

events.name: Fundamental lemma
events.summary: Ngo proved the fundamental lemma by interpreting orbital integrals through the geometry of Hitchin fibration.
keyWorks: Ngo, Le lemme fondamental pour les algebres de Lie, Publ.IHES 2010
events.verifierNotes: Ngo arXiv 0801.0446 (Publ. IHES 2010) confirmed. Langlands-Shelstad stated the lemma in 1987; Laumon-Ngo 2004 and Ngo 2008 brought in the geometry.

events.name: Kervaire invariant one
events.summary: Hill, Hopkins and Ravenel used equivariant methods to show Kervaire invariant one manifolds exist only in dimensions 2,6,14,30,62 and possibly 126.
keyWorks: Hill-Hopkins-Ravenel, On the nonexistence of elements of Kervaire invariant one, Annals 2016
events.verifierNotes: HHR, arXiv:0908.3724 (Annals 2016), confirmed. Equivariant stable homotopy settled a differential-topology problem.

events.name: Higher topos theory
events.summary: Quasicategory-based infinity-topoi and derived geometry reframed homotopy theory and moduli problems.
keyWorks: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Princeton 2009
Toen-Vezzosi, Homotopical algebraic geometry I and II, 2005-08
events.verifierNotes: Lurie HTT arXiv math/0608040 (2006, book 2009) confirmed; Toen-Vezzosi HAG I/II run from 2002 (Adv. Math 2005, Memoirs 2008).

events.name: Neural tangent kernel
events.summary: Infinite-width networks were analysed as kernel machines and mean fields.
keyWorks: Jacot, Gabriel, Hongler, Neural tangent kernel, arXiv:1806.07572
events.verifierNotes: Jacot-Gabriel-Hongler, arXiv:1806.07572, confirmed. Duplicate of WC95. Borderline: an established correspondence from wide networks to kernels and Wasserstein gradient flows (Mei-Montanari-Nguyen, Chizat-Bach 2018).

events.name: Virtual Haken
events.summary: Special cube complexes and hierarchy methods showed hyperbolic 3-manifolds virtually fibre, resolving Thurston's questions.
keyWorks: Wise, The structure of groups with a quasiconvex hierarchy, 2011
Agol, The virtual Haken conjecture, Doc. Math. 2013
events.verifierNotes: Agol, Doc. Math. 18 (2013), arXiv 2012; Wise hierarchy preprint 2009-11 (book 2021); Haglund-Wise special cube complexes 2008. 1982 is Thurston question, not the bridge.

events.name: Fourier analysis for density problems (Roth)
events.summary: A circle-method style Fourier argument with a density-increment iteration shows dense integer sets contain three-term progressions.
keyWorks: K. F. Roth, On certain sets of integers, J. London Math. Soc. 28 (1953)
W. T. Gowers, A new proof of Szemeredi's theorem, Geom. Funct. Anal. 11 (2001)

events.name: The Langlands programme: automorphic forms and Galois representations over number fields
events.summary: Galois representations are conjecturally matched with automorphic representations, linking arithmetic, representation theory and harmonic analysis.
keyWorks: R. P. Langlands, letter to A. Weil (January 1967)
R. P. Langlands, Problems in the theory of automorphic forms, in Lectures in Modern Analysis and Applications III, Lecture Notes in Math. 170 (1970)
H. Jacquet and R. P. Langlands, Automorphic Forms on GL(2), Lecture Notes in Math. 114 (1970)
J. Tate, Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (1950; in Cassels-Frohlich, Algebraic Number Theory, 1967)
M. Harris and R. Taylor, The Geometry and Cohomology of Some Simple Shimura Varieties, Annals of Math. Studies 151 (2001)
B. C. Ngo, Le lemme fondamental pour les algebres de Lie, Publ. Math. IHES 111 (2010) 1-169

events.name: Unipotent flows and the Oppenheim conjecture
events.summary: Values of indefinite quadratic forms at integer points are controlled by showing orbits of unipotent subgroups on homogeneous spaces are well-behaved.
keyWorks: G. A. Margulis, Indefinite quadratic forms and unipotent flows on homogeneous spaces, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I 304 (1987)
M. Ratner, On Raghunathan's measure conjecture, Ann. of Math. 134 (1991)

events.name: Topology proves Kneser's conjecture
events.summary: The chromatic number of Kneser graphs is bounded below via the Borsuk-Ulam theorem applied to a topological space built from the graph.
keyWorks: L. Lovasz, Kneser's conjecture, chromatic number, and homotopy, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 25 (1978)
I. Barany, A short proof of Kneser's conjecture, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 25 (1978)

events.name: Gauge theory transforms four-manifold topology
events.summary: Solutions of the Yang-Mills and later Seiberg-Witten equations give invariants distinguishing smooth structures on four-manifolds, results unreachable by classical topology.
keyWorks: S. K. Donaldson, An application of gauge theory to four-dimensional topology, J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983)
M. H. Freedman, The topology of four-dimensional manifolds, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982)
E. Witten, Monopoles and four-manifolds, Math. Res. Lett. 1 (1994)

events.name: Stability theory in diophantine geometry (Hrushovski)
events.summary: Stability-theoretic results about definable groups prove the Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields and give a model-theoretic proof of Manin-Mumford.
keyWorks: E. Hrushovski, The Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 9 (1996)
E. Hrushovski, The Manin-Mumford conjecture and the model theory of difference fields, Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 112 (2001) 43-115

events.name: The polynomial method in combinatorics
events.summary: Low-degree polynomials vanishing on a point set give short proofs of the finite-field Kakeya problem and the Erdos distinct-distances problem in the plane.
keyWorks: Z. Dvir, On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 22 (2009)
L. Guth and N. H. Katz, On the Erdos distinct distances problem in the plane, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015)

events.name: Hyperbolic geometry enters three-manifold topology (Thurston)
events.summary: Three-manifolds are decomposed into pieces carrying one of eight model geometries, hyperbolic being generic, so topology is studied with geometric tools.
keyWorks: W. P. Thurston, Three-dimensional manifolds, Kleinian groups and hyperbolic geometry, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 6 (1982) 357-381
W. P. Thurston, Three-Dimensional Geometry and Topology, vol. 1 (1997)

events.name: Computers enter proof: four colour theorem and the Kepler conjecture
events.summary: Exhaustive case analysis by computer is accepted as proof in graph theory, and later whole proofs are re-verified in proof assistants.
keyWorks: K. Appel and W. Haken, Every planar map is four colorable. Part I: Discharging, Illinois J. Math. 21 (1977) 429-490
K. Appel, W. Haken and J. Koch, Every planar map is four colorable. Part II: Reducibility, Illinois J. Math. 21 (1977) 491-567
G. Gonthier, Formal proof - the four-color theorem, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 55 (2008) 1382-1393
T. Hales et al., A formal proof of the Kepler conjecture, Forum Math. Pi 5 (2017) e2

events.name: Ramsey-theoretic dichotomies in Banach space theory
events.summary: Infinite Ramsey theory and descriptive set theory are used to prove dichotomies for Banach spaces and to construct spaces answering the unconditional basic sequence problem.
keyWorks: W. T. Gowers and B. Maurey, The unconditional basic sequence problem, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1993) 851-874
W. T. Gowers, A new dichotomy for Banach spaces, Geom. Funct. Anal. 6 (1996) 1083-1093

events.name: Sullivan's dictionary: rational maps and Kleinian groups
events.summary: Iteration of rational maps is matched term by term with the theory of Kleinian groups, so results and techniques of one side suggest and prove statements on the other.
keyWorks: D. Sullivan, Conformal dynamical systems, in Geometric Dynamics (Rio de Janeiro 1981), Lecture Notes in Math. 1007 (1983) 725-752
D. Sullivan, Quasiconformal homeomorphisms and dynamics I: Solution of the Fatou-Julia problem on wandering domains, Ann. of Math. 122 (1985) 401-418
C. T. McMullen, Complex Dynamics and Renormalization, Annals of Math. Studies 135 (1994)

events.name: Random partitions, representation theory and Gromov-Witten theory
events.summary: Measures on partitions defined by Schur functions are analysed as determinantal point processes, and the same structures compute Gromov-Witten and Hurwitz invariants.
keyWorks: A. Okounkov, Infinite wedge and random partitions, Selecta Math. (N.S.) 7 (2001) 57-81
A. Okounkov and R. Pandharipande, Gromov-Witten theory, Hurwitz theory, and completed cycles, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 517-560

events.name: Measure rigidity and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity
events.summary: Entropy and measure-rigidity methods for diagonal group actions show that Hecke eigenfunctions on arithmetic surfaces do not concentrate, a quantum chaos statement.
keyWorks: E. Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 165-219

events.name: Hardness versus randomness
events.summary: Explicit combinatorial designs turn a function hard for small circuits into a generator fooling small circuits, linking circuit lower bounds and derandomisation.
keyWorks: N. Nisan and A. Wigderson, Hardness vs randomness, Proc. 29th IEEE FOCS (1988); J. Comput. System Sci. 49 (1994) 149-167
R. Impagliazzo and A. Wigderson, P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits: derandomizing the XOR lemma, Proc. 29th ACM STOC (1997) 220-229

events.name: Concentration of measure
events.summary: Isoperimetric inequalities in high dimension give sharp deviation bounds for Lipschitz functions, used for Banach space geometry and probability in product spaces.
keyWorks: V. D. Milman, A new proof of A. Dvoretzky's theorem on cross-sections of convex bodies, Funct. Anal. Appl. 5 (1971) 28-37
M. Talagrand, Concentration of measure and isoperimetric inequalities in product spaces, Publ. Math. IHES 81 (1995) 73-205

events.name: Spin glasses: the Parisi formula
events.summary: A replica-symmetry-breaking prediction for the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model is proved by interpolation arguments and ultrametricity.
keyWorks: G. Parisi, Infinite number of order parameters for spin-glasses, Phys. Rev. Lett. 43 (1979) 1754-1756
F. Guerra, Broken replica symmetry bounds in the mean field spin glass model, Comm. Math. Phys. 233 (2003) 1-12
M. Talagrand, The Parisi formula, Ann. of Math. 163 (2006) 221-263

events.name: Superrigidity and arithmeticity of lattices
events.summary: Ergodic-theoretic arguments on homogeneous spaces force lattices in higher rank semisimple groups to be arithmetic, tying Lie theory, ergodic theory and number theory.
keyWorks: G. A. Margulis, Discrete groups of motions of manifolds of nonpositive curvature, Proc. ICM Vancouver 1974, vol. 2 (1975) 21-34
G. A. Margulis, Discrete Subgroups of Semisimple Lie Groups (1991)

events.name: Virtual fundamental cycles via homotopical algebra
events.summary: Homotopy-coherent methods give a rigorous construction of virtual fundamental cycles on moduli spaces of pseudoholomorphic curves, underpinning Floer and Fukaya theory.
keyWorks: J. Pardon, An algebraic approach to virtual fundamental cycles on moduli spaces of pseudo-holomorphic curves, Geom. Topol. 20 (2016) 779-1034

events.name: Dynamical systems and spectral theory of Schrodinger operators
events.summary: Renormalisation and cocycle dynamics are used to describe the spectrum of quasi-periodic Schrodinger operators, solving the Ten Martini type problems.
keyWorks: A. Avila, Global theory of one-frequency Schrodinger operators, Acta Math. 215 (2015) 1-54

events.name: Periodic torus orbits, subconvexity and homogeneous dynamics
events.summary: Equidistribution of torus orbits on homogeneous spaces and subconvex bounds for L-functions are combined to prove equidistribution theorems for arithmetic objects.
keyWorks: M. Einsiedler, E. Lindenstrauss, P. Michel and A. Venkatesh, Distribution of periodic torus orbits on homogeneous spaces, Duke Math. J. 148 (2009) 119-174
P. Michel and A. Venkatesh, The subconvexity problem for GL_2, Publ. Math. IHES 111 (2010) 171-271

events.name: Machine-assisted discovery in knot theory and representation theory
events.summary: DeepMind used neural networks to suggest a relation between signature and hyperbolic invariants of knots and a combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.
keyWorks: Davies et al., Advancing mathematics by guiding human intuition with AI, Nature 2021
events.verifierNotes: Davies et al., Nature 600 (2021). ML-guided conjecture discovery; knot signature/slope relation later proved. Borderline methodological import; medium.

events.name: AKS primality
from: algebra of polynomial rings over finite fields
events.summary: Agrawal, Kayal and Saxena gave an unconditional deterministic polynomial-time primality test using polynomial congruences.
keyWorks: Agrawal-Kayal-Saxena, PRIMES is in P, Annals 2004
events.verifierNotes: AKS, Annals 160 (2004), preprint Aug 2002. Elementary algebra settles a complexity question; bridge is modest, so medium.

events.name: Vassiliev invariants
events.summary: Knot invariants were filtered by order via singular knots, unifying Jones-type polynomials into a finite-type theory.
keyWorks: Vassiliev, Cohomology of knot spaces, 1990
Bar-Natan, On the Vassiliev knot invariants, Topology 1995
Kontsevich, Vassiliev's knot invariants, 1993
events.verifierNotes: Vassiliev 1990; Kontsevich integral 1993; Bar-Natan, Topology 34 (1995).

events.name: Topological recursion and enumerative geometry
events.summary: Eynard-Orantin recursion recovers Gromov-Witten and Weil-Petersson volumes.
keyWorks: Eynard, Orantin, Invariants of algebraic curves and topological expansion, 2007, arXiv:math-ph/0702045
events.verifierNotes: Eynard-Orantin math-ph/0702045, CNTP 1 (2007).

events.name: Heegaard Floer and Seiberg-Witten theory
events.summary: Seiberg-Witten monopole equations gave simpler four-manifold invariants than Donaldson's, and Ozsvath-Szabo later built a Floer theory of Heegaard diagrams.
keyWorks: Witten, Monopoles and four-manifolds, Math.Res.Lett. 1994
Ozsvath-Szabo, Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds, Annals 2004
events.verifierNotes: Bundles two events: Seiberg-Witten import 1994 (Witten MRL 1994) and Heegaard Floer 2001 (arXiv math/0101206, Annals 159 2004). Recommend splitting.

events.name: Quantum information theory as a field (Shor, Grover, error correction)
events.summary: Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover search gave a mathematical programme of quantum algorithms and codes.
keyWorks: Shor, Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization, SIAM J. Comput. 1997
Grover, A fast quantum mechanical algorithm, STOC 1996
events.verifierNotes: Shor FOCS 1994, SIAM J. Comput. 26 (1997). Conceptual dates Feynman 1982 / Deutsch 1985 are out of scope; methodological 1994 is in.

events.name: Natural proofs and algebrization barriers
events.summary: Meta-theorems explained why known techniques fail to separate P and NP.
keyWorks: Razborov-Rudich, Natural proofs, JCSS 1997
Aaronson-Wigderson, Algebrization, TOCT 2009
events.verifierNotes: Razborov-Rudich STOC 1994, JCSS 55 (1997); Aaronson-Wigderson 2008. Both are inside TCS, so the bridge is borderline.

events.name: Elliptic curve and pairing-based cryptography
events.summary: Weil/Tate pairings on elliptic curves enabled new cryptographic protocols such as identity-based encryption.
keyWorks: Boneh-Franklin, Identity-based encryption from the Weil pairing, CRYPTO 2001
Joux, A one round protocol for tripartite Diffie-Hellman, 2000
events.verifierNotes: Boneh-Franklin CRYPTO 2001 (SIAM J. Comput. 2003) checked. ECC itself is from 1985 and out of scope; the in-scope event is pairing-based crypto (MOV 1993 attack, then Joux / Sakai-Ohgishi-Kasahara 2000).

events.name: CAT(0) cube complexes in geometric group theory
events.summary: Sageev and Haglund-Wise linked cube complexes with group actions, giving linearity and separability results.
keyWorks: Sageev, Ends of group pairs and non-positively curved cube complexes, 1995
Haglund, Wise, Special cube complexes, GAFA 2008
events.verifierNotes: Sageev Proc. LMS 1995 checked; Haglund-Wise GAFA 2008 linked cube complexes to RAAGs. Gromov 1987 is a precursor. Overlaps QC48.

events.name: Categorification as programme
events.summary: Crane-Frenkel proposed categorifying quantum groups; Khovanov-Lauda and Rouquier gave concrete versions.
keyWorks: Crane, Frenkel, Four-dimensional topological quantum field theory, Hopf categories, J. Math. Phys. 1994
Khovanov, Lauda, A diagrammatic approach to categorification, 2008
events.verifierNotes: Khovanov-Lauda appeared in Represent. Theory 2009 (arXiv 2008), not 2008. Crane-Frenkel 1994 coined the programme; Khovanov homology 1999 was its first deliberate use.

events.name: Boolean function analysis / invariance principle (Mossel-O'Donnell-Oleszkiewicz)
events.summary: An invariance principle transferred Gaussian results to low-influence Boolean functions, used to settle majority-is-stablest.
keyWorks: Mossel, O'Donnell, Oleszkiewicz, Noise stability of functions with low influences, Annals 2010, arXiv:math/0503503
events.verifierNotes: MOO arXiv math/0503503, Annals 2010 checked. Gaussian probability (Borell) transferred to Boolean functions proves Majority is Stablest.

events.name: Thurston-Perelman to Kahler-Einstein: K-stability
events.summary: Chen-Donaldson-Sun proved Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, equating K-stability with Kahler-Einstein metrics.
keyWorks: Chen, Donaldson, Sun, Kahler-Einstein metrics on Fano manifolds I-III, JAMS 2015
events.verifierNotes: CDS I-III JAMS 2015 (online 2014) checked. The name is misleading, since Perelman is not involved. The dictionary runs through Yau 1993, Tian 1997 and Donaldson 2002.

events.name: Liouville quantum gravity and mating of trees
to: random planar geometry / Liouville quantum gravity
events.summary: Duplantier-Sheffield-Miller-Gwynne built random surfaces from Gaussian free field and linked them to SLE.
keyWorks: Duplantier, Miller, Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity as a mating of trees, arXiv:1409.7055
events.verifierNotes: DMS arXiv 1409.7055 checked. Duplantier-Sheffield KPZ (arXiv 2008, Invent. 2011) is the earlier conceptual start.

events.name: Ergodic theory and Littlewood conjecture
events.summary: Measure rigidity of diagonal actions gave partial resolution of Littlewood's conjecture and quantum unique ergodicity for arithmetic surfaces.
keyWorks: Einsiedler-Katok-Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture, Annals 2006
Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity, Annals 2006
events.verifierNotes: EKL Annals 2006 checked. Measure rigidity for higher-rank actions (Katok-Spatzier 1996) gives a measure-zero exceptional set for Littlewood. The Margulis-Oppenheim 1987 bridge is an earlier precursor.

events.name: Amplituhedron and positive geometry
events.summary: Arkani-Hamed-Trnka represented amplitudes as volumes of a geometric object.
keyWorks: Arkani-Hamed, Trnka, The amplituhedron, arXiv:1312.2007
events.verifierNotes: Arkani-Hamed-Trnka arXiv 1312.2007, JHEP 2014 checked. The mathematical follow-up is Arkani-Hamed-Bai-Lam 2017 and Galashin-Lam.

events.name: Sato-Tate conjecture
events.summary: Potential automorphy of symmetric powers gave equidistribution of Frobenius angles of elliptic curves.
keyWorks: Clozel-Harris-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts, Publ.IHES 2008
Barnet-Lamb-Geraghty-Harris-Taylor, A family of Calabi-Yau varieties and potential automorphy II, 2011
events.verifierNotes: Barnet-Lamb-Geraghty-Harris-Taylor PRIMS 2011 checked. The first key work is misattributed: CHT 2008 Publ. IHES is Clozel-Harris-Taylor, and HSBT is Harris-Shepherd-Barron-Taylor Annals 2010. The conceptual date is out of scope.

events.name: Inverse theorem for Gowers norms and Mobius-nilsequences
to: analytic number theory (linear equations in primes)
events.summary: Green-Tao-Ziegler proved nilsequences control Gowers norms, settling linear equations in primes counts.
keyWorks: Green, Tao, Ziegler, An inverse theorem for the Gowers U^{s+1} norm, Annals 2012, arXiv:1009.3998
events.verifierNotes: GTZ Annals 2012, arXiv 1009.3998 checked. Nilsequences from ergodic theory enter additive number theory. Overlaps QC1.

events.name: Restricted Burnside problem
events.summary: Zelmanov used Lie ring methods to show finitely many finite quotients exist for exponent n.
keyWorks: Zelmanov, Solution of the restricted Burnside problem for groups of odd exponent, Math USSR Izv. 1991
events.verifierNotes: Zel'manov, Math USSR Izv. 36 (1991) checked (Russian 1990). Builds on Kostrikin's Lie-ring reduction of 1959, which is out of scope; Zelmanov's 1989-91 solution is in scope.

events.name: Lorentzian polynomials and log-concavity
events.summary: A class of polynomials unifies log-concavity statements across matroids, Hodge theory and discrete convex analysis, giving the strongest Mason conjecture.
keyWorks: Branden-Huh, Lorentzian polynomials, Annals 2020 (arXiv:1902.03719)
events.verifierNotes: Branden-Huh arXiv 1902.03719 (Feb 2019) confirmed; abstracts Hodge-theoretic log-concavity into a polynomial class used for Mason-type conjectures.

events.name: Floer theory and Fukaya categories (Lagrangian Floer)
events.summary: Lagrangian intersection Floer theory was organised into an A-infinity category; Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono gave a rigorous foundation.
keyWorks: Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, Lagrangian intersection Floer theory, AMS/IP 2009
events.verifierNotes: FOOO AMS/IP 2009 (Crossref 2010) confirmed. Floer's 1988 Floer homology is out of scope; the in-scope part is Fukaya's 1993 A-infinity category, used by Kontsevich's 1994 homological mirror symmetry.

events.name: Shor's algorithm
events.summary: Polynomial-time quantum factoring and discrete logarithm via the quantum Fourier transform created the field of quantum algorithms and cryptanalysis.
keyWorks: Shor, Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer, SIAM J.Comput. 1997 (quant-ph/9508027)
events.verifierNotes: Shor FOCS/LNCS 1994 and SIAM J. Comput. 1997 confirmed.

events.name: Kitaev's topological quantum computation
from: topological quantum field theory / modular tensor categories
events.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons used modular tensor categories and links to Jones-type invariants.
keyWorks: Kitaev, Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons, Ann.Phys. 2003 (quant-ph/9707021)
Freedman-Kitaev-Larsen-Wang, Topological quantum computation, BAMS 2003
events.verifierNotes: Kitaev quant-ph/9707021 (Ann. Phys. 2003) confirmed; FKLW BAMS 2003 also exists.

events.name: Paracontrolled distributions
events.summary: Paraproduct calculus gave an alternative to regularity structures for singular SPDEs.
keyWorks: Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski, Paracontrolled distributions and singular PDEs, Forum Math Pi 2015
events.verifierNotes: GIP Forum Math Pi 2015 confirmed (arXiv 1210.2684, 2012).

events.name: SYZ conjecture
events.summary: Mirror pairs were conjectured to be dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations, giving a geometric picture of mirror symmetry.
keyWorks: Strominger-Yau-Zaslow, Mirror symmetry is T-duality, Nucl.Phys.B 1996 (hep-th/9606040)
events.verifierNotes: SYZ Nucl. Phys. B 1996 confirmed. The conjecture is open in general, but the framework drives the Gross-Siebert programme.

events.name: Exotic spheres, smooth Poincare in dimension 4 ... Floer to Heegaard
events.summary: Embedded contact homology proved the Weinstein conjecture in dimension 3.
keyWorks: Taubes, The Seiberg-Witten equations and the Weinstein conjecture, Geom. Topol. 2007, arXiv:math/0611007
events.verifierNotes: Taubes G&T 2007 (10.2140/gt.2007.11.2117) confirmed. The name and dates are garbled: the event is the 3D Weinstein conjecture via Seiberg-Witten theory, 2006-07.

events.name: MIP* = RE: Connes embedding refuted
events.summary: Quantum interactive proof results showed entangled provers decide the halting problem, which refutes Connes' embedding conjecture.
keyWorks: Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, Yuen, MIP*=RE, arXiv:2001.04383
events.verifierNotes: arXiv 2001.04383 and CACM 2021 confirmed. The full paper is still not formally refereed after a fix, but the result is widely accepted as established.

events.name: Random matrix universality and Dyson / Tracy-Widom in KPZ
events.summary: Longest increasing subsequence fluctuations were shown to follow Tracy-Widom, linking random permutations to random matrices.
keyWorks: Baik-Deift-Johansson, On the distribution of the length of the longest increasing subsequence, JAMS 1999
Okounkov, Infinite wedge and random partitions, Selecta 2001
events.verifierNotes: BDJ JAMS 1999 and Okounkov Selecta 2001 confirmed; Johansson 2000 linked it to growth models.

events.name: Learning with errors and lattice cryptography
events.summary: Regev's LWE gave worst-case to average-case reductions and a quantum reduction from lattice problems.
keyWorks: Ajtai, Generating hard instances of lattice problems, STOC 1996
Regev, On lattices, learning with errors, random linear codes and cryptography, STOC 2005
events.verifierNotes: Regev STOC 2005 / JACM 2009 confirmed. Ajtai STOC 1996 (worst-case to average-case) is well known but was not separately looked up.

events.name: Seiberg-Witten invariants
events.summary: Witten's physical dual to Donaldson theory gave monopole equations that quickly proved the Thom conjecture.
keyWorks: Witten, Monopoles and four-manifolds, Math. Res. Lett. 1994, arXiv:hep-th/9411102
events.verifierNotes: Witten MRL 1994 (10.4310/mrl.1994.v1.n6.a13) confirmed.

events.name: Graph limits and graphons
events.summary: Dense graph sequences were given analytic limit objects, unifying extremal combinatorics and statistical physics.
keyWorks: Lovasz-Szegedy, Limits of dense graph sequences, JCTB 2006
Lovasz, Large Networks and Graph Limits, AMS 2012
events.verifierNotes: Lovasz-Szegedy arXiv math/0408173 (2004; JCTB 2006) confirmed.

events.name: Kashiwara crystal bases
events.summary: Crystal bases give combinatorial skeleton of quantum group representations.
keyWorks: Kashiwara, On crystal bases of the q-analogue of universal enveloping algebras, Duke 1991
events.verifierNotes: Kashiwara CMP 1990 and Duke 1991 confirmed.

events.name: Okounkov-Reshetikhin probabilistic representation theory
events.summary: Random partitions and Schur processes were used to analyse asymptotics and Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas theory.
keyWorks: Okounkov-Reshetikhin, Correlation function of Schur process, JAMS 2003
Okounkov-Pandharipande, GW/DT correspondences, 2006
events.verifierNotes: Okounkov-Reshetikhin JAMS 2003 confirmed. The GW/DT correspondence (MNOP 2006) is a separate event.

events.name: Topological modular forms
events.summary: A spectrum of topological modular forms links the elliptic curve moduli stack to stable homotopy groups.
keyWorks: Hopkins, Algebraic topology and modular forms, ICM 2002 (math/0212397)
events.verifierNotes: Hopkins ICM 2002, math/0212397, confirmed. TMF itself (Hopkins-Miller) dates from about 1994; elliptic cohomology from 1986-88 is a precursor.

events.name: Heegaard Floer homology
events.summary: Ozsvath and Szabo defined invariants of three-manifolds by Lagrangian Floer theory on Heegaard diagrams.
keyWorks: Ozsvath, Szabo, Holomorphic disks and topological invariants, Annals 2004, arXiv:math/0101206
events.verifierNotes: Ozsvath-Szabo, math/0101206 (2001; Annals 2004), confirmed. Lagrangian Floer theory joined to Heegaard diagrams of 3-manifolds.

events.name: Kontsevich-Soibelman wall crossing
events.summary: Wall-crossing formulas for DT invariants unify stability conditions and cluster transformations.
keyWorks: Kontsevich-Soibelman, Stability structures, motivic DT invariants and cluster transformations, 2008 (arXiv:0811.2435)
events.verifierNotes: Kontsevich-Soibelman, arXiv:0811.2435 (2008), confirmed. Joins DT invariants, stability conditions and cluster transformations.

events.name: Derived algebraic geometry
events.summary: Toen-Vezzosi and Lurie combined algebraic geometry with homotopical algebra to build derived schemes.
keyWorks: Toen, Vezzosi, Homotopical algebraic geometry II, Memoirs AMS 2008
Lurie, Derived Algebraic Geometry, thesis 2004
events.verifierNotes: Toen-Vezzosi HAG II, math/0404373 (Memoirs 2008), confirmed. Precursors: Kontsevich's hidden smoothness (1994) and Ciocan-Fontanine-Kapranov (2001).

events.name: Differential privacy
events.summary: Dwork-McSherry-Nissim-Smith defined privacy through noise calibration.
keyWorks: Dwork, McSherry, Nissim, Smith, Calibrating noise to sensitivity, TCC 2006
events.verifierNotes: Dwork-McSherry-Nissim-Smith, TCC 2006 (LNCS), confirmed. Dinur-Nissim 2003 is a precursor. A TCS field, mathematical in nature.

events.name: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance
events.summary: Quantum codes and the threshold theorem showed reliable quantum computation is possible with noisy gates.
keyWorks: Shor, Scheme for reducing decoherence in quantum computer memory, PRA 1995
Calderbank-Shor, Good quantum error-correcting codes exist, PRA 1996
Aharonov-Ben-Or, Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant error, 1997
events.verifierNotes: Shor, PRA 52 (1995); Calderbank-Shor, quant-ph/9512032; Aharonov-Ben-Or, quant-ph/9611025: all confirmed. Classical coding theory carried into quantum mechanics.

events.name: Hodge theory via o-minimality
events.summary: Bakker-Klingler-Tsimerman used o-minimal definability for Ax-Schanuel and algebraicity of period maps.
keyWorks: Bakker, Klingler, Tsimerman, Tame topology of arithmetic quotients, JAMS 2019, arXiv:1810.04801
events.verifierNotes: BKT, arXiv:1810.04801, confirmed; it appeared in JAMS 33 (2020), not 2019. Model theory settling Hodge-theoretic algebraicity. Pila-Zannier 2008 is the earlier o-minimal/diophantine bridge.

events.name: Flag algebras
events.summary: Razborov turned Turan-type problems into semidefinite programs using limits of graph densities.
keyWorks: Razborov, Flag algebras, J.Symbolic Logic 2007
events.verifierNotes: Razborov, Flag algebras, J. Symbolic Logic 2007, confirmed. Semidefinite programming joined to extremal graph theory.

events.name: Kakeya and Bourgain-Guth, decoupling for Vinogradov
events.summary: Bourgain-Demeter-Guth proved the main Vinogradov mean-value conjecture using l^2 decoupling from harmonic analysis.
keyWorks: Bourgain, Demeter, Guth, Proof of the main conjecture in Vinogradov's mean value theorem, Annals 2016, arXiv:1512.01565
events.verifierNotes: BDG, arXiv:1512.01565 (Annals 2016), confirmed. Builds on Bourgain-Demeter l^2 decoupling (Annals 2015). The name's 'Kakeya and Bourgain-Guth' is misleading.

events.name: Kapustin-Witten: geometric Langlands as S-duality
events.summary: Twisted N=4 super Yang-Mills was used to derive Hecke eigensheaves from branes.
keyWorks: Kapustin, Witten, Electric-magnetic duality and the geometric Langlands program, arXiv:hep-th/0604151
events.verifierNotes: Kapustin-Witten, hep-th/0604151, confirmed. S-duality of N=4 SYM imported into geometric Langlands.

events.name: Geometrization of local Langlands (Fargues-Scholze)
events.summary: Fargues and Scholze built a moduli of G-bundles on the Fargues-Fontaine curve to attach L-parameters to representations.
keyWorks: Fargues, Scholze, Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence, arXiv:2102.13459
events.verifierNotes: Fargues-Scholze, arXiv:2102.13459, confirmed. Fargues stated the conjecture in 2014-16; the result is accepted by experts.

events.name: Bourgain: harmonic analysis meets number theory and dispersive PDE
events.summary: Fourier restriction spaces X^{s,b} gave global well-posedness for periodic dispersive equations.
keyWorks: Bourgain, Fourier transform restriction phenomena for certain lattice subsets and applications to nonlinear evolution equations, GAFA 1993
events.verifierNotes: Bourgain, GAFA 3 (1993), parts I and II, confirmed. Lattice-point and exponential-sum estimates applied to periodic dispersive PDE.

events.name: Tropical geometry
events.summary: Algebraic varieties were replaced by piecewise-linear shadows, allowing enumerative problems to be solved by counting combinatorial objects.
keyWorks: Mikhalkin, Enumerative tropical algebraic geometry in R^2, JAMS 2005
Itenberg-Mikhalkin-Shustin, Tropical Algebraic Geometry, 2007
Maclagan-Sturmfels, Introduction to Tropical Geometry, 2015
events.verifierNotes: Mikhalkin, math/0312530 (2003; JAMS 2005), confirmed. Tropical counting of plane curves.

events.name: Kadison-Singer via interlacing polynomials
events.summary: Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava solved Kadison-Singer using interlacing families of polynomials, a method arising from graph sparsification.
keyWorks: Marcus, Spielman, Srivastava, Interlacing families II, Annals 2015, arXiv:1306.3969
events.verifierNotes: MSS, arXiv:1306.3969 (Annals 2015), confirmed. A tool from spectral graph theory and real-rooted polynomials settled an operator-algebra problem: a technique transfer, not an import.

events.name: Graph theory birth
events.summary: Kirchhoff's circuit trees, Cayley's tree counting, and the four colour problem made graphs a subject, with Koenig's 1936 book as first textbook.
keyWorks: Kirchhoff, Ueber die Aufloesung der Gleichungen, 1847
Cayley, On the theory of the analytical forms called trees, 1857
Kuratowski, Sur le probleme des courbes gauches en topologie, 1930

events.name: Riemannian geometry
events.summary: Riemann generalised Gauss's intrinsic surface geometry to n-dimensional manifolds with a metric, making curvature an intrinsic notion.
keyWorks: Riemann, Ueber die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen, 1854 (publ. 1868)

events.name: General relativity and tensor geometry
events.summary: Riemannian geometry and the tensor calculus are adopted as the language of gravitation, then fed back as a source of problems for geometry and analysis.

events.name: Tensor calculus (Ricci)
events.summary: Christoffel and Ricci developed coordinate-independent calculus of tensors, systematised by Ricci and Levi-Civita.
keyWorks: Christoffel, Ueber die Transformation der homogenen Differentialausdruecke, Crelle 1869
Ricci and Levi-Civita, Methodes de calcul differentiel absolu, Math. Ann. 1900

events.name: Ideals and algebraic number theory
events.summary: Dedekind replaced Kummer's ideal numbers by sets of algebraic integers closed under addition and multiplication, restoring unique factorization.
keyWorks: Dedekind, supplement X to Dirichlet's Vorlesungen ueber Zahlentheorie, 2nd ed. 1871; 3rd ed. 1879

events.name: Riemann surfaces
events.summary: Riemann treated multi-valued algebraic functions as single-valued functions on a covering surface, bringing topology into complex analysis.
keyWorks: Riemann, Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen, 1851
Riemann, Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, 1857
Weyl, Die Idee der Riemannschen Flaeche, 1913

events.name: Cantor's set theory
events.summary: Cantor's study of exceptional sets for trigonometric series led to countability, uncountability of the reals, and then transfinite ordinals and cardinals.
keyWorks: Cantor, Ueber eine Eigenschaft des Inbegriffes aller reellen algebraischen Zahlen, Crelle 1874
Cantor, Grundlagen einer allgemeinen Mannigfaltigkeitslehre, 1883

events.name: Erlangen programme
events.summary: Klein defined a geometry by the group of transformations leaving its properties invariant.
keyWorks: Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen ueber neuere geometrische Forschungen, 1872

events.name: Lie theory
events.summary: Lie combined contact transformations with integration theory of PDE to build continuous transformation groups and infinitesimal generators.
keyWorks: Lie, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen I-III, with Engel, 1888-93

events.name: Poincare's algebraic topology
events.summary: Poincare introduced homology and the fundamental group as algebraic invariants of manifolds.
keyWorks: Poincare, Analysis situs, J. Ecole Polytechnique 1895
Poincare, Complements a l'Analysis situs, 1899-1904

events.name: Commutative algebra from invariant theory and ideals
events.summary: Noether used chain conditions to treat primary decomposition and unique ideal factorization for abstract rings.
keyWorks: Noether, Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen, Math. Ann. 1921
Noether, Abstrakter Aufbau der Idealtheorie in algebraischen Zahl- und Funktionenkoerpern, 1926

events.name: Invariant theory and Hilbert basis theorem
events.summary: Gordan proved finite generation of binary invariants by hard computation, and Hilbert's abstract basis theorem settled the general case non-constructively, shifting algebra toward structure.
keyWorks: Gordan, Beweis, dass jede Covariante ... eine endliche Anzahl ... besitzt, 1868
Hilbert, Ueber die Theorie der algebraischen Formen, Math. Ann. 1890

events.name: Volterra functionals
events.summary: Volterra introduced functionals as functions of functions, and Hadamard named the field in 1910.
keyWorks: Volterra, Sopra le funzioni che dipendono da altre funzioni, 1887
Hadamard, Lecons sur le calcul des variations, 1910

events.name: Hilbert space and integral equations
from: quadratic forms in infinitely many variables
events.summary: Hilbert and Riesz made sequence and function spaces into an infinite-dimensional geometry with spectral theory.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Grundzuege einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen, 1904-1910
Riesz, Sur les systemes orthogonaux de fonctions, 1907

events.name: Banach spaces
events.summary: Banach defined complete normed spaces and proved the key theorems on operators, forming the Lwow school.
keyWorks: Banach, Sur les operations dans les ensembles abstraits, Fund. Math. 1922
Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires, 1932
