events.name: Metric spaces (Frechet)
events.summary: Frechet unified earlier function-space work by Cantor, Volterra, Arzela and Hadamard into abstract metric spaces.
keyWorks: Frechet, Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, 1906

events.name: Measure-theoretic probability
events.summary: Borel, Lebesgue, Kolmogorov applied measure theory to probability.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung, 1933

events.name: Lebesgue measure and integration
events.summary: Jordan, Borel and Lebesgue built measure on sets and defined an integral that behaves well under limits.
keyWorks: Borel, Lecons sur la theorie des fonctions, 1898
Lebesgue, Integrale, longueur, aire, 1902

events.name: Group theory in quantum mechanics
events.summary: Symmetry groups of atoms and spectra are analysed by decomposing the state space into irreducible representations, which also drives the general theory.

events.name: Hilbert-space quantum mechanics
to: abstract Hilbert space and unbounded operator theory
events.summary: Matrix and wave mechanics were unified in the Hilbert-space framework by Weyl, Dirac and von Neumann.
keyWorks: Weyl, Gruppentheorie und Quantenmechanik, 1928
von Neumann, Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik, 1932

events.name: Ergodic theory
events.summary: Boltzmann's ergodic hypothesis became a rigorous theorem when Birkhoff and von Neumann used Lebesgue measure and Hilbert space.
keyWorks: Birkhoff, Proof of the ergodic theorem, PNAS 1931
von Neumann, Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis, 1932

events.name: Number fields / function fields dictionary
events.summary: Dedekind and Weber applied ideal theory to function fields of Riemann surfaces, giving an algebraic proof of Riemann-Roch.
keyWorks: Dedekind and Weber, Theorie der algebraischen Functionen einer Veraenderlichen, Crelle 1882

events.name: Game theory
events.summary: Zermelo, Borel and von Neumann treated games mathematically and proved minimax.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele, Math. Ann. 1928

events.name: Riemann zeta and prime number theorem
events.summary: Riemann treated the prime-counting problem through the zeta function as a complex-analytic object, opening a path from complex analysis to the distribution of primes.
keyWorks: Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse, 1859

events.name: Circle method
events.summary: Hardy, Ramanujan and Littlewood used contour integrals to count partitions and Waring representations.
keyWorks: Hardy and Ramanujan, Asymptotic formulae in combinatory analysis, 1918
Hardy and Littlewood, Partitio numerorum, 1920-28

events.name: Brownian motion
events.summary: Bachelier, Einstein and Smoluchowski modelled random motion probabilistically, and Wiener later gave it a rigorous measure.
keyWorks: Bachelier, Theorie de la speculation, 1900
Einstein, Ueber die von der molekularkinetischen Theorie ... geforderte Bewegung, Ann. Phys. 1905
Wiener, Differential-space, 1923

events.name: Automorphic functions and uniformisation
events.summary: Poincare and Klein linked discrete groups of Mobius transformations, hyperbolic geometry and differential equations, and uniformised algebraic curves.
keyWorks: Poincare, Theorie des groupes fuchsiens, Acta Math. 1882
Klein and Fricke, Vorlesungen ueber die Theorie der automorphen Functionen, 1897-1912

events.name: Dynamical systems from celestial mechanics
events.summary: Poincare studied orbits geometrically rather than by formulae, uncovering homoclinic phenomena in the three-body problem, and Birkhoff built on this.
keyWorks: Poincare, Sur les courbes definies par une equation differentielle, 1881-86
Poincare, Les methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste, 1892-99
Birkhoff, Dynamical Systems, 1927

events.name: Lyapunov stability
events.summary: Lyapunov gave general criteria for stability of equilibria using auxiliary functions.
keyWorks: Lyapunov, The General Problem of the Stability of Motion, 1892

events.name: Geometry of numbers
events.summary: Minkowski used convex bodies to attack Diophantine and quadratic form problems.
keyWorks: Minkowski, Geometrie der Zahlen, 1896-1910

events.name: Boolean algebra of logic
events.summary: Boole, Peirce and Schroeder treated logic as an algebra of classes and relations.
keyWorks: Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought, 1854
Schroeder, Vorlesungen ueber die Algebra der Logik, 1890-95

events.name: Markov chains
events.summary: Markov studied dependent trials and showed the law of large numbers extends to chains, later applying them to letter sequences.
keyWorks: Markov, Extension of the law of large numbers to dependent quantities, 1906

events.name: Hilbert's programme
events.summary: Hilbert proposed to prove consistency of mathematics by finitary methods.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Axiomatisches Denken, 1918
Hilbert and Ackermann, Grundzuege der theoretischen Logik, 1928

events.name: Cartan exterior differential calculus
events.summary: Cartan developed the exterior derivative and used it with Pfaffian systems and moving frames to unify differential geometry with Lie theory.
keyWorks: Cartan, Sur certaines expressions differentielles et le probleme de Pfaff, 1899
Cartan, Lecons sur les invariants integraux, 1922

events.name: Affine connections (Levi-Civita, Weyl)
events.summary: Levi-Civita introduced parallel transport, Weyl generalised to gauge geometry, and Cartan developed connections and moving frames.
keyWorks: Levi-Civita, Nozione di parallelismo in una varieta qualunque, 1917
Weyl, Gravitation und Elektrizitaet, 1918

events.name: Arithmetization and construction of the reals
events.summary: Weierstrass, Cantor and Dedekind defined real numbers from rationals via limits or cuts, removing reliance on geometric intuition.
keyWorks: Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872
Cantor, Ueber die Ausdehnung eines Satzes aus der Theorie der trigonometrischen Reihen, Math. Ann. 1872

events.name: Frege predicate logic
events.summary: Frege invented quantified predicate logic and tried to derive arithmetic from it.
keyWorks: Frege, Begriffsschrift, 1879
Frege, Grundgesetze der Arithmetik, 1893-1903

events.name: Peano arithmetic axioms
events.summary: Dedekind and Peano gave axioms characterizing the natural numbers, Peano in formal logical notation.
keyWorks: Dedekind, Was sind und was sollen die Zahlen, 1888
Peano, Arithmetices principia, 1889

events.name: Biometric mathematical statistics
events.summary: Pearson developed correlation and chi-square for biological data and founded Biometrika.
keyWorks: Pearson, Mathematical Contributions to the Theory of Evolution, 1893-1912

events.name: Fisher statistical inference
events.summary: Fisher unified chi-squared, small-sample t and variance analysis into a framework tested on Rothamsted crop data.
keyWorks: Fisher, The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance, 1918
Fisher, Statistical Methods for Research Workers, 1925
Fisher, The Design of Experiments, 1935

events.name: Killing-Cartan classification
events.summary: Killing and Cartan decomposed semisimple Lie algebras into simple ones and classified them into four families plus exceptional cases.
keyWorks: Killing, Die Zusammensetzung der stetigen endlichen Transformationsgruppen, Math. Ann. 1888-90
Cartan, thesis, 1894

events.name: General topology (Hausdorff)
events.summary: Hausdorff's Grundzuege gave neighborhood axioms for topological spaces.
keyWorks: Hausdorff, Grundzuege der Mengenlehre, 1914

events.name: Vector analysis
events.summary: Gibbs and Heaviside extracted vector methods from quaternions.
keyWorks: Gibbs, Elements of Vector Analysis, 1881-84; Wilson, Vector Analysis, 1901

events.name: Italian algebraic geometry
events.summary: Castelnuovo, Enriques and Severi classified algebraic surfaces up to birational equivalence with geometric methods lacking rigorous foundations.
keyWorks: Castelnuovo and Enriques, Sulle condizioni di razionalita dei piani doppi, 1896
Enriques, Introduzione alla geometria sopra le superficie algebriche, 1896

events.name: Model theory beginnings
events.summary: Loewenheim and Skolem showed that first-order theories with infinite models have countable ones, opening semantic study of formal theories.
keyWorks: Loewenheim, Ueber Moeglichkeiten im Relativkalkuel, Math. Ann. 1915
Skolem, Logisch-kombinatorische Untersuchungen, 1920

events.name: Axiomatic set theory (Zermelo)
events.summary: Zermelo proved well-ordering from choice and axiomatized set theory.
keyWorks: Zermelo, Beweis dass jede Menge wohlgeordnet werden kann, 1904
Zermelo, Untersuchungen ueber die Grundlagen der Mengenlehre I, 1908

events.name: Minkowski spacetime
events.summary: Minkowski reformulated special relativity as geometry of four dimensions.
keyWorks: Minkowski, Raum und Zeit, 1909

events.name: Abstract group concept
events.summary: Cayley, Kronecker, Weber and von Dyck gradually axiomatised groups independently of permutations, ending with the full modern definition.
keyWorks: Cayley, On the theory of groups, Phil. Mag. 1854
von Dyck, Gruppentheoretische Studien, Math. Ann. 1882
Schmidt, Abstract Theory of Groups, 1916

events.name: Brouwer topology
events.summary: Brouwer used simplicial approximation and degree to prove invariance of dimension and the fixed-point theorem.
keyWorks: Brouwer, Beweis der Invarianz der Dimensionszahl, Math. Ann. 1911
Brouwer, Ueber Abbildung von Mannigfaltigkeiten, Math. Ann. 1912

events.name: Noether's theorem
events.summary: Noether tied continuous symmetries of an action to conserved quantities, answering questions in general relativity.
keyWorks: Noether, Invariante Variationsprobleme, Nachr. Goettingen 1918

events.name: Representation theory of finite groups
events.summary: Frobenius, Burnside and Schur studied groups through matrix representations, and character tables proved structural theorems such as Burnside's p^a q^b.
keyWorks: Frobenius, Ueber Gruppencharaktere, 1896
Burnside, On the theory of groups of finite order, 1897; Theory of Groups of Finite Order, 1897
Schur, Neue Begruendung der Theorie der Gruppencharaktere, 1905

events.name: Matrix algebra
events.summary: Sylvester named matrices and Cayley gave their algebra, with product and inverse.
keyWorks: Cayley, A memoir on the theory of matrices, Phil. Trans. 1858
Sylvester, Additions to the articles on a new class of theorems, Phil. Mag. 1850

events.name: Class field theory
events.summary: Abelian extensions of number fields were matched to ideal-class-type groups, from Kronecker, Weber and Hilbert through Takagi's existence theorem and Artin's reciprocity law.
keyWorks: Takagi, Ueber eine Theorie des relativ Abel'schen Zahlkoerpers, 1920
Artin, Beweis des allgemeinen Reziprozitaetsgesetzes, 1927

events.name: Heaviside operational calculus
events.summary: Heaviside treated differentiation as an algebraic operator to solve telegraph and circuit equations, later justified through Laplace transforms.
keyWorks: Heaviside, Electromagnetic Theory, 1893-1912

events.name: Axiomatisation of geometry
events.summary: Hilbert gave a complete independent axiom system for Euclidean geometry that did not rely on diagrams, and used models to test independence.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Grundlagen der Geometrie, 1899

events.name: Intuitionism
events.summary: Brouwer rejected the unrestricted law of excluded middle.
keyWorks: Brouwer, Over de Grondslagen der Wiskunde, thesis 1907
Heyting, Die formalen Regeln der intuitionistischen Logik, 1930

events.name: p-adic numbers
events.summary: Hensel treated integers like power series in a prime, giving p-adic numbers, and Kuerschak and Hasse later turned this into valuation theory and local-global principles.
keyWorks: Hensel, Ueber eine neue Begruendung der Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen, 1899
Hensel, Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen, 1908

events.name: Ramsey theory
events.summary: Ramsey proved a combinatorial theorem on homogeneous subsets while studying a decision problem in logic, and van der Waerden proved a related Ramsey-type theorem on arithmetic progressions.
keyWorks: Ramsey, On a problem of formal logic, Proc. LMS 1930
van der Waerden, Beweis einer Baudetschen Vermutung, 1927

events.name: Functional analysis
events.summary: Integral equations and the calculus of variations are treated as linear algebra in infinite-dimensional normed spaces with topological structure.

events.name: Distributions: from Dirac's delta to generalised functions
events.summary: Objects used formally by physicists (the delta function) are given a rigorous home as continuous functionals on test functions, which becomes the basis of modern PDE.

events.name: Deriving the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics
events.summary: Hilbert's sixth-problem programme of deriving kinetic equations from Newtonian particle systems is carried to long times for hard spheres.

events.name: Representations of compact and continuous groups (Schur, Weyl, Peter-Weyl)
events.summary: Schur and Weyl used invariant integration to extend finite-group representation theory to compact Lie groups.
keyWorks: Weyl, Theorie der Darstellung kontinuierlicher halbeinfacher Gruppen, Math. Z. 1925-26
Peter and Weyl, Die Vollstaendigkeit der primitiven Darstellungen, 1927

events.name: Weyl's gauge theory
events.summary: Weyl proposed local scale invariance.
keyWorks: Weyl, Gravitation und Elektrizitaet, 1918

events.name: Geometric (Clifford) algebra
events.summary: Clifford fused Hamilton's quaternions and Grassmann's exterior algebra into a single geometric algebra.
keyWorks: Clifford, Applications of Grassmann's Extensive Algebra, Am. J. Math. 1878

events.name: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and algebraic geometry as ideal theory
events.summary: Hilbert linked ideals of polynomials to geometric zero sets, starting the algebraisation of algebraic geometry.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Ueber die vollen Invariantensysteme, Math. Ann. 1893

events.name: Homology groups (Noether) and algebraic topology
events.summary: Noether's insight that Betti numbers are ranks of groups moved topology toward group-valued invariants, and the field was renamed accordingly.
keyWorks: Hopf, Eine Verallgemeinerung der Euler-Poincareschen Formel, 1928
Lefschetz, Algebraic Topology, 1942

events.name: Rigorous foundations of algebraic geometry via commutative algebra
events.summary: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil used valuation and ideal theory to rebuild the Italian school's results rigorously.
keyWorks: van der Waerden, Zur algebraischen Geometrie I-III, Math. Ann. 1933-
Zariski, Algebraic Surfaces, 1935

events.name: Structure of associative algebras (Wedderburn)
events.summary: Cartan, Frobenius and Molien decomposed algebras over C, and Wedderburn extended this to arbitrary fields.
keyWorks: Wedderburn, On Hypercomplex Numbers, Proc. LMS 1907

events.name: Betti numbers and early combinatorial topology
events.summary: Riemann's connectivity of surfaces was extended by Betti to higher-dimensional spaces via numerical invariants.
keyWorks: Betti, Sopra gli spazi di un numero qualunque di dimensioni, 1871

events.name: Transcendence proofs for e and pi
events.summary: Liouville, Hermite and Lindemann used analytic constructions to show specific numbers are not algebraic, settling squaring the circle.
keyWorks: Hermite, Sur la fonction exponentielle, 1873
Lindemann, Ueber die Zahl pi, Math. Ann. 1882

events.name: Differential Galois theory
events.summary: Picard and Vessiot carried the Galois correspondence to linear differential equations, with Lie groups replacing finite groups.
keyWorks: Picard, Sur les equations differentielles lineaires, 1883
Vessiot, Sur la theorie de Galois et ses diverses generalisations, 1904

events.name: Russell paradox, type theory and Principia Mathematica
events.summary: Russell's paradox led to the ramified theory of types and the formal derivation of mathematics.
keyWorks: Russell, The Principles of Mathematics, 1903
Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica, 1910-13

events.name: Steinitz abstract field theory
events.summary: Steinitz gave the first abstract definition of field and proved every field has an algebraic closure.
keyWorks: Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Koerper, Crelle 1910

events.name: Calculus of variations to Hilbert's direct methods
events.summary: Hilbert justified Dirichlet's principle with direct variational methods, rescuing Riemann's use of minimisation in complex analysis.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Ueber das Dirichletsche Princip, 1900

events.name: Fredholm integral equations
events.summary: Fredholm treated integral equations as limits of linear algebraic systems and solved the Dirichlet problem.
keyWorks: Fredholm, Sur une nouvelle methode pour la resolution du probleme de Dirichlet, 1900
Fredholm, Sur une classe d'equations fonctionnelles, Acta Math. 1903

events.name: Borel sets and measure
events.summary: Borel introduced a hierarchy of sets generated from open sets and applied countable additivity.
keyWorks: Borel, Lecons sur la theorie des fonctions, 1898

events.name: Many-valued logics
events.summary: Lukasiewicz and Post independently defined logics with more than two truth values.
keyWorks: Lukasiewicz, O logice trojwartosciowej, 1920
Post, Introduction to a general theory of elementary propositions, Am. J. Math. 1921

events.name: Godel's completeness and incompleteness theorems
events.summary: Godel arithmetized syntax inside number theory to show undecidable sentences.
keyWorks: Godel, Die Vollstaendigkeit der Axiome des logischen Funktionenkalkuels, 1930
Godel, Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze, 1931

events.name: Frobenius method and singular ODE theory
events.summary: Fuchs and Frobenius used series in the complex domain to solve linear ODEs with regular singular points.
keyWorks: Fuchs, Zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen, 1866
Frobenius, Ueber die Integration der linearen Differentialgleichungen durch Reihen, 1873

events.name: Wiener process
events.summary: Wiener constructed rigorous measure on Brownian paths.
keyWorks: Wiener, Differential space, J. Math. Phys. 1923

events.name: Several complex variables and Hartogs
events.summary: Hartogs discovered phenomena, such as automatic extension of holomorphic functions, with no one-variable analogue.
keyWorks: Hartogs, Zur Theorie der analytischen Funktionen mehrerer unabhaengiger Veraenderlichen, 1906

events.name: Abstract rings and fields
events.summary: Dedekind, Weber, Steinitz and Fraenkel gave axiomatic definitions of fields and rings, culminating in van der Waerden's textbook.
keyWorks: Weber, Die allgemeinen Grundlagen der Galois'schen Gleichungstheorie, Math. Ann. 1893
Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Koerper, Crelle 1910
van der Waerden, Moderne Algebra, 1930-31

events.name: Decision problems for groups (Dehn)
events.summary: Dehn posed word, conjugacy and isomorphism problems for finitely presented groups, motivated by topology.
keyWorks: Dehn, Ueber unendliche diskontinuierliche Gruppen, Math. Ann. 1911

events.name: Operator algebras
events.summary: Von Neumann introduced self-adjoint operator algebras.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Algebra der Funktionaloperationen, Math. Ann. 1929-30

events.name: Descriptive set theory
events.summary: Baire, Lebesgue, Suslin and Lusin explored regularity of definable sets, leading to analytic and projective sets.
keyWorks: Suslin, Sur une definition des ensembles measurables B, 1917
Lusin, Lecons sur les ensembles analytiques, 1930

events.name: Schur: polynomial representations of GL(n) and invariant theory
events.summary: Schur's thesis used Frobenius methods to classify rational representations of the general linear group, tying them to symmetric functions.
keyWorks: Schur, Ueber eine Klasse von Matrizen, die sich einer gegebenen Matrix zuordnen lassen, thesis 1901

events.name: Klein model: consistency of non-Euclidean geometry within projective geometry
events.summary: Klein showed Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries are special cases of projective geometry with a conic, making them equally consistent.
keyWorks: Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 1871 and 1873
Cayley, A sixth memoir upon quantics, 1859

events.name: Peano's vector space axioms
events.summary: Peano gave a modern axiomatic definition of vector space after Grassmann.
keyWorks: Peano, Calcolo geometrico, 1888

events.name: Riemann-Hilbert problem and monodromy
events.summary: Riemann asked for a differential equation with prescribed monodromy group, and Plemelj attacked it with singular integral equations.
keyWorks: Plemelj, Riemannsche Funktionenscharen mit gegebener Monodromiegruppe, Monatsh. Math. 1908

events.name: Weyl's Riemann surface and abstract manifold concept
events.summary: Weyl gave a rigorous definition of Riemann surface as a topological manifold with charts.
keyWorks: Weyl, Die Idee der Riemannschen Flaeche, 1913

events.name: Noncommutative algebras, representation theory and number theory
from: algebraic number theory (class field theory, p-adic local theory)
events.summary: Noether, Brauer and Hasse linked hypercomplex systems to commutative algebra and arithmetic via modules and cohomological ideas.
keyWorks: Brauer, Hasse, Noether, Beweis eines Hauptsatzes in der Theorie der Algebren, Crelle 1932

events.name: Dirichlet principle: potential theory as a tool for function theory
events.summary: Riemann used a variational minimum principle from potential theory to guarantee existence of functions on surfaces; Weierstrass's criticism led to Hilbert's repaired form.
keyWorks: Riemann, thesis 1851
Hilbert, Ueber das Dirichletsche Princip, 1901

events.name: Mathematical biology
events.summary: Volterra and Lotka modeled predator-prey dynamics.
keyWorks: Volterra, Variazioni e fluttuazioni, 1926

events.name: Subjective probability and decision
events.summary: Keynes, Ramsey and de Finetti defined probability as degree of belief, reviving Bayesian ideas against frequentism.
keyWorks: Keynes, A Treatise on Probability, 1921
Ramsey, Truth and Probability, 1926
de Finetti, Funzione caratteristica di un fenomeno aleatorio, 1930

events.name: Hasse local-global principle
events.summary: Hasse showed a quadratic form represents zero over the rationals when it does so over all completions.
keyWorks: Hasse, Ueber die Darstellbarkeit von Zahlen durch quadratische Formen im Koerper der rationalen Zahlen, Crelle 1923

events.name: Consistency models of non-Euclidean geometry
events.summary: Beltrami and Klein built models of hyperbolic geometry inside Euclidean or projective geometry, showing the parallel postulate independent of the other axioms.
keyWorks: Beltrami, Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea, 1868
Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 1871

events.name: Combinatorial group theory and presentations
events.summary: Von Dyck and then Dehn, Nielsen and Schreier studied groups by generators and relations, motivated by fundamental groups of surfaces and knots.
keyWorks: Dehn, Ueber unendliche diskontinuierliche Gruppen, Math. Ann. 1911
Schreier, Die Untergruppen der freien Gruppen, 1927

events.name: Burnside's use of character theory for finite group theory
events.summary: Burnside applied Frobenius characters to prove the p^a q^b solvability theorem.
keyWorks: Burnside, Theory of Groups of Finite Order, 1897 and 2nd ed. 1911
Burnside, On groups of order p^a q^b, 1904

contestedOnly.name: Fast Fourier transform
contestedOnly.summary: An N log N algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform was published.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Algorithmic advance within numerical analysis (Gauss precedent); Math. Comp. 19 (1965) confirmed.

contestedOnly.name: Constructible universe
contestedOnly.summary: Inner model L showed AC and CH consistent with ZF.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Godel PNAS 1938 and Annals Study 3 (1940) verified; internal to set theory/logic. Duplicate of WB4.

contestedOnly.name: Cybernetics
contestedOnly.summary: Feedback, communication and statistics were fused into a theory of control in animals and machines.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Cybernetics (Wiley 1948) confirmed. Interdisciplinary science programme rather than a mathematical field; the mathematical core (Wiener filtering, 1942/1949) could be catalogued separately.

contestedOnly.name: Neyman-Pearson testing
contestedOnly.summary: Tests are framed as optimal decisions between hypotheses with error rates and power.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Neyman-Pearson, Phil. Trans. A 1933 confirmed. Birth of the theory of hypothesis testing; mostly internal to statistics.

contestedOnly.name: Small cancellation theory
contestedOnly.summary: Combinatorial diagram arguments with curvature solve word problems.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Tartakovskii 1949, Greendlinger 1960, Lyndon 1966 (van Kampen diagrams). Lyndon-Schupp book confirmed (1977; Crossref reprint 2001). Modest bridge.

contestedOnly.name: Chaos theory in dynamical systems
contestedOnly.summary: Lorenz's computer experiments reveal sensitive dependence; Smale and others formalise.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: J. Atmos. Sci. 1963 confirmed. The mathematical uptake came via Ruelle-Takens 1971 and Li-Yorke 1975.

contestedOnly.name: Nash-De Giorgi regularity
contestedOnly.summary: Hoelder continuity for elliptic and parabolic equations with rough coefficients was proved, settling Hilbert's 19th problem.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Nash AJM 1958 confirmed (and PNAS 1957 note). De Giorgi 1957 imports measure-theoretic/isoperimetric methods into elliptic regularity to settle Hilbert's 19th problem (calculus of variations). Borderline: analysis-internal.

contestedOnly.name: Experimental design
contestedOnly.summary: Randomisation and factorial structure are formalised for inference.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Fisher 1935 book confirmed (Open Library). Conceptual start is Fisher 1926, 'The arrangement of field experiments', before 1930; the 1935 book is in scope. An agricultural import that became a statistics subfield.

contestedOnly.name: Multi-armed bandits and sequential design
contestedOnly.summary: Robbins formalises adaptive allocation between uncertain options.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Robbins, Bull. AMS 1952 confirmed; Thompson 1933 is the precursor. A narrow subfield; Wald's sequential analysis (1945-47) is the larger neighbouring event.

contestedOnly.name: Martingale theory
contestedOnly.summary: Fair-game processes became a core tool.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Doob 1953 confirmed (Open Library). Ville 1939 gives the name and the gambling origin. Subfield birth within probability.

contestedOnly.name: Graph minors theory
contestedOnly.summary: Kuratowski planarity is generalised to minor ordering (Robertson-Seymour).
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Robertson-Seymour, JCTB 1983 confirmed. The conceptual date should be 1983, with Kuratowski 1930 and Wagner 1937 as precursors. Surface topology into structural graph theory.

contestedOnly.name: Pontryagin classes and cohomology ops
contestedOnly.summary: Stiefel, Whitney, Chern, Pontryagin define bundle invariants.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Real birth of characteristic classes (Stiefel, Whitney 1935; Pontryagin 1942). Chern Annals 1946 verified. The name's 'cohomology ops' is wrong.

contestedOnly.name: Kepler / Flyspeck
contestedOnly.summary: Hales gave a computer-assisted proof and the Flyspeck project produced a formal verification in HOL Light and Isabelle.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Hales Annals 2005 and Flyspeck arXiv 1501.02155 (Forum Math Pi 2017) checked. Not an import from outside: LP and computer verification settle a geometry problem. Flyspeck is a formalisation milestone, not a field birth.

contestedOnly.name: Geometric deep learning
contestedOnly.summary: Equivariance to symmetry groups and graph or manifold structure was used to unify neural architecture design.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Bronstein et al. arXiv 2104.13478; Cohen-Welling ICML 2016. Representation theory enters ML through equivariance; applied, so low-medium.

contestedOnly.name: Random matrix universality
contestedOnly.summary: Local spectral statistics were shown universal for generalised Wigner matrices by relaxation of Dyson Brownian motion and by replacement methods.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: ESY arXiv 0907.5605, Invent. 2011; Tao-Vu arXiv 0906.0510, Acta 2011. Dyson Brownian motion and swapping are internal to RMT and probability.

contestedOnly.name: Fully homomorphic encryption
contestedOnly.summary: Gentry built the first fully homomorphic scheme from ideal lattices, followed by LWE-based schemes.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Gentry STOC 2009 checked. FHE is an internal cryptographic construction on an already-imported lattice bridge. The real bridge event is Ajtai 1996 (worst-case lattice problems to cryptography) or Regev 2005 (LWE).

contestedOnly.name: Expander graphs: zig-zag product and SL=L
contestedOnly.summary: Zig-zag products of graphs gave explicit expanders and Reingold's log-space connectivity.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: RVW zig-zag (FOCS 2000, Annals 155 2002); Reingold JACM 55 (2008). Expanders in complexity date from the 1980s; group theory is not a source. Internal TCS advance.

contestedOnly.name: Density Hales-Jewett via ergodic/combinatorial fusion
contestedOnly.summary: Furstenberg-Katznelson extended ergodic Ramsey methods to a density version of Hales-Jewett; Polymath gave a combinatorial proof.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Furstenberg-Katznelson J. Anal. Math. 1991 checked. It applies Furstenberg's 1977 ergodic-Ramsey bridge; the Polymath 2009 combinatorial proof is internal.

contestedOnly.name: Szemeredi regularity and hypergraph removal
contestedOnly.summary: Gowers and independently Rodl-Skokan and Nagle-Rodl-Schacht extended regularity to hypergraphs, yielding a combinatorial proof of Szemeredi for all progression lengths.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Gowers Annals 2007 checked. Hypergraph regularity is internal to extremal combinatorics: a combinatorial re-proof of an ergodic theorem, with no new bridge.

contestedOnly.name: Four-colour theorem formalised in Coq
contestedOnly.summary: Gonthier reformalised the four-colour theorem in Coq, removing reliance on unchecked code.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Gonthier's Coq four-colour proof (Notices AMS 2008; LNCS 2008 version on Crossref) checks an existing proof in an existing field. A formalisation milestone, not a new bridge.

contestedOnly.name: Stochastic differential equations for diffusion models
contestedOnly.summary: Score-based generative models were recast through reverse-time SDEs.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Song et al. arXiv 2011.13456 (ICLR 2021) confirmed. Uses existing SDE/Fokker-Planck theory in machine learning, so it is an application rather than a new mathematical area.

contestedOnly.name: Symplectic field theory
contestedOnly.summary: Holomorphic-curve invariants were assembled into an algebraic framework for contact manifolds and cobordisms.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: EGH GAFA Visions 2000 confirmed. It is mainly a framework inside symplectic/contact topology (holomorphic curves extended to contact boundaries), so it is not clearly a cross-field birth.

contestedOnly.name: Modularity theorem completion
contestedOnly.summary: Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor extended modularity to all elliptic curves over the rationals.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: BCDT JAMS 2001 confirmed. It completes Wiles' method; the bridge (Frey-Ribet-Wiles) dates to 1985-95.

contestedOnly.name: Feit-Thompson formalised
contestedOnly.summary: A Coq team formalised the odd order theorem with the ssreflect library, showing large proofs can be verified.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Gonthier et al. ITP 2013 confirmed. Formal verification of an existing theorem.

contestedOnly.name: AI-assisted mathematics (AlphaProof, FunSearch)
contestedOnly.summary: Neural nets proposed conjectures in knot theory and proofs at olympiad level.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Davies et al. Nature 2021 confirmed and gave refereed theorems (a knot signature inequality, Kazhdan-Lusztig progress). Borderline because it is close to a trend; date it by the Nature paper.

contestedOnly.name: Categorical geometric Langlands proof
contestedOnly.summary: Arinkin-Gaitsgory reformulation was proved by Gaitsgory and collaborators.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Arinkin-Gaitsgory, Selecta 2015 (online 2014), and Gaitsgory-Raskin et al., arXiv:2405.03599, confirmed. A landmark proof but internal to geometric Langlands, whose tools were already joined.

contestedOnly.name: Geometric Langlands to Hitchin: Higgs bundles and non-abelian Hodge
contestedOnly.summary: Simpson and Hitchin related Higgs bundles to local systems, later tied to Langlands and mirror symmetry.
contestedOnly.verdictNotes: Simpson, Publ. IHES 75 (1992), confirmed. The correspondence comes from Hitchin, Donaldson, Corlette and Simpson in 1987-88. The Langlands link (Hausel-Thaddeus 2003, Donagi-Pantev) is a separate event.
